evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a respiratory, blood, liver, and bladder pathogen of significant clinical concern.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a pathogen that causes respiratory, blood, liver, and bladder infections and is a significant clinical concern.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a type of bacteria that can cause life-threatening infections – including pneumonia, blood stream infections, and urinary tract infections – in hospitalized patients.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a bacterium that can cause serious infections in various parts of the body, including the lungs, bloodstream, liver, and bladder.
allowed_evidence_spans: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a respiratory , blood , liver , and bladder pathogen of significant clinical concern .

Klebsiella pneumoniae is an opportunistic Gram-negative pathogen that can cause a wide range of life-threatening infections , including pneumonia , sepsis and urinary tract infections ( Bengoechea and Sa Pessoa , 2019; Paczosa and Mecsas , 2016; European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control , 2018; Weiner et al . , 2016 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The adaptor protein, SKAP2, is required for protection against K. pneumoniae pulmonary infections.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The adaptor protein SKAP2 is necessary for protection against Klebsiella pneumoniae pulmonary infections.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: But the role of this protein in fighting K. pneumoniae infections is not clear.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study investigated the role of SKAP2, an adaptor protein, in the body's defense against lung infections caused by K. pneumoniae.
allowed_evidence_spans: We show that the adaptor protein , SKAP2 , is required for protection against K . pneumoniae ( ATCC 43816 ) pulmonary infections .
Using a murine model of K . pneumoniae 43816 infection , we characterized the role of SKAP2 in pulmonary host defense against K . pneumoniae in this study .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: This study characterized the role of SKAP2 in pulmonary host defense against K. pneumoniae using a murine model.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Using a murine model of K . pneumoniae 43816 infection , we characterized the role of SKAP2 in pulmonary host defense against K . pneumoniae in this study .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Skap2-/- mice had 100-fold higher bacterial burden when compared to wild-type and burden was controlled by SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Mice lacking SKAP2 (Skap2-/- mice) had 100-fold higher bacterial burden compared to wild-type mice during Klebsiella pneumoniae infection, and SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells controlled this burden.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Mice lacking SKAP2 in their white blood cells had more bacteria in their lungs than normal mice.
evidence_rows.lay_context: In experiments with mice, those without SKAP2 had significantly more bacteria in their lungs, indicating that SKAP2, particularly in innate immune cells, helps control the infection.
allowed_evidence_spans: Skap2-/- mice had 100-fold higher bacterial burden when compared to wild-type and burden was controlled by SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells .
burden was controlled by SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells .

Combined, these data indicate Skap2 expression in BM-derived immune cells is required to contain K. pneumoniae growth during lung infection, and that Skap2 expression in cells that are not derived from the marrow do not contribute to this phenotype.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Mice lacking SKAP2 (Skap2-/- mice) had 100-fold higher bacterial burden compared to wild-type mice during Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Skap2-/- mice had 100-fold higher bacterial burden when compared to wild-type and burden was controlled by SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: SKAP2 expression in bone marrow-derived immune cells is required to contain Klebsiella pneumoniae growth during lung infection in mice.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Combined, these data indicate Skap2 expression in BM-derived immune cells is required to contain K. pneumoniae growth during lung infection, and that Skap2 expression in cells that are not derived from the marrow do not contribute to this phenotype.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: K. pneumoniae-stimulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in vitro was abolished in Skap2-/- neutrophils, while neutrophils degranulated normally.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Klebsiella pneumoniae-stimulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production was abolished in Skap2-/- neutrophils in vitro, but their degranulation in response to K. pneumoniae infection was normal.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: But neutrophils without the protein do not [produce a burst of chemicals called “reactive oxygen species”].
evidence_rows.lay_context: While neutrophils without SKAP2 were still present in infected lungs and could degranulate normally, they completely lost the ability to produce reactive oxygen species (ROS) when stimulated by K. pneumoniae in laboratory tests.
allowed_evidence_spans: K . pneumoniae-stimulated reactive oxygen species ( ROS ) production in vitro was abolished .
This suggests that the increased in susceptibility of Skap2-/- mice was not due to defects in degranulation .

SKAP2 was indispensable for K . pneumoniae-stimulated neutrophil ROS production , but not degranulation or phagocytosis , suggesting that the increased bacterial burden in the Skap2-/- mice is affected by the loss of ROS .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Klebsiella pneumoniae-stimulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production was abolished in Skap2-/- neutrophils in vitro.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: K . pneumoniae-stimulated reactive oxygen species ( ROS ) production in vitro was abolished .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: K. pneumoniae-induced neutrophil ROS response required the activity of SFKs, Syk, Btk, PLCγ2, and PKC.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in neutrophils, induced by K. pneumoniae, required the activity of SFKs, Syk, Btk, PLCγ2, and PKC.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study identified several key proteins—SFKs, Syk, Btk, PLCγ2, and PKC—whose activity was necessary for neutrophils to produce reactive oxygen species in response to K. pneumoniae.
allowed_evidence_spans: This suggests SFKs , Syk , Btk , PLCγ2 , and PKC are each necessary for K . pneumoniae-activated ROS production .

Src family kinases ( SFKs ) , Spleen Associated Tyrosine Kinase ( Syk ) , Bruton’s tyrosine kinase ( Btk ) , Phospholipase Cγ2 ( PLCγ2 ) , and PKC play critical roles in receptor-mediated ROS production ( Löfgren et al . , 1999; Braselmann et al . , 2006; Volmering et al . , 2016; Dang et al . , 2001; Raad et al . , 2009; Kovács et al . , 2014; Fumagalli et al . , 2007; Graham et al . , 2007; Nguyen et al . , 2017 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The loss of SKAP2 significantly hindered the K. pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs, Syk, and Pyk2, implicating SKAP2 as proximal to their activation in pathogen-signaling pathways.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The absence of SKAP2 significantly impaired the K. pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs, Syk, and Pyk2, suggesting that SKAP2 is an early component in their activation within pathogen-signaling pathways.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Without SKAP2, several proteins that help produce reactive oxygen species do not work.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that without SKAP2, the activation (phosphorylation) of key proteins like SFKs, Syk, and Pyk2 was significantly reduced, positioning SKAP2 as an important early step in the immune signaling pathway against K. pneumoniae.
allowed_evidence_spans: The loss of SKAP2 significantly hindered the K . pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs , Syk , and Pyk2 implicating SKAP2 as proximal to their activation in pathogen-signaling pathways .
The loss of SKAP2 significantly hindered the K . pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs , Syk , and Pyk2 implicating SKAP2 as proximal to their activation in pathogen-signaling pathways .

Collectively , these results show that SFKs , Syk , and Pyk2 are required for K . pneumoniae-stimulated ROS production , and that the loss of SKAP2 prevents full phosphorylation of SFKs , Syk , and Pyk2 after K . pneumoniae stimulation such that neutrophils are unable to generate ROS production .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The loss of SKAP2 significantly hindered the Klebsiella pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs, Syk, and Pyk2.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: The loss of SKAP2 significantly hindered the K . pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs , Syk , and Pyk2 implicating SKAP2 as proximal to their activation in pathogen-signaling pathways .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: SKAP2-dependent signaling in neutrophils is essential for K. pneumoniae-activated ROS production and for promoting bacterial clearance during infection.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: SKAP2-dependent signaling in neutrophils is essential for both Klebsiella pneumoniae-activated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and for promoting bacterial clearance during infection.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Understanding the role of SKAP2 in fighting infections may help scientists better understand the immune system.
evidence_rows.lay_context: In conclusion, the study highlights that SKAP2's signaling role in neutrophils is crucial for generating reactive oxygen species to fight K. pneumoniae and for effectively clearing the bacteria during an infection.
allowed_evidence_spans: SKAP2-dependent signaling in neutrophils is essential for K . pneumoniae-activated ROS production and for promoting bacterial clearance during infection .
SKAP2-dependent signaling in neutrophils is essential for K . pneumoniae-activated ROS production and for promoting bacterial clearance during infection .
Together, these data indicate that neutrophils cannot control K. pneumoniae 43816 infection in the absence of SKAP2 in the hematopoietic compartment.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur following activation of latent liver-stages parasites (hypnozoites) causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur when latent liver-stage parasites, called hypnozoites, activate, causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: P. vivax is dangerous because it causes recurring malaria due to hypnozoites.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Plasmodium vivax malaria is characterized by recurring infections, known as relapses. These relapses happen when dormant forms of the parasite, called hypnozoites, activate in the liver and cause new infections in the blood, often weeks or months after the first infection.
allowed_evidence_spans: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur following activation of latent liver-stages parasites ( hypnozoites ) causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: P. vivax is the deadliest malaria

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We develop a within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites, and validate it against data from tropical strains of P. vivax.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: A within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites was developed and validated against data from tropical strains of P. vivax.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: A mathematical model was developed to understand P. vivax transmission, accounting for hypnozoites.
evidence_rows.lay_context: To better understand P. vivax, researchers created a mathematical model that simulates the behavior of hypnozoites within an infected individual. This model was tested and confirmed using real data from P. vivax strains found in tropical regions.
allowed_evidence_spans: We develop a within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites , and validate it against data from tropical strains of P . vivax .

In this manuscript , a within-host model of hypnozoites in liver hepatocytes is developed to demonstrate that many of the epidemiological patterns of relapse infections can be explained by making the assumption that hypnozoites activate and die at a constant rate .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: the model covers all malaria types

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The within-host relapse model was fitted to data on time to first relapse infection from three ecological zones: South America, South East Asia, and Melanesia.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Figure 1 shows the best fit within-host relapse model to data on time to first relapse infection from three ecological zones with tropical strains of P . vivax: South America , South East Asia and Melanesia ( Battle et al . , 2014 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The within-host model is embedded in a P. vivax transmission model to demonstrate the build-up of the hypnozoite reservoir following new infections and its depletion through hypnozoite activation and death.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The within-host model was integrated into a P. vivax transmission model to show how the hypnozoite reservoir builds up after new infections and depletes through activation and death.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The model accounts for the hypnozoite reservoir, assuming constant activation and death rates.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This within-host model was then incorporated into a larger P. vivax transmission model. This allowed researchers to simulate how the pool of hypnozoites in the liver grows after new infections and shrinks as hypnozoites activate to cause relapses or die.
allowed_evidence_spans: The within-host model is embedded in a P . vivax transmission model to demonstrate the build-up of the hypnozoite reservoir following new infections and its depletion through hypnozoite activation and death .
We next embedded the within-host model for tropical relapses in a model for the transmission of P . vivax between humans and mosquitoes ( Figure 8 ) .

Following infection with a tropical strain of P . vivax , the population dynamics of hypnozoites in the liver can be described by a within-host model where each hypnozoite is subject to two processes: ( i ) activation leading to relapse infection; and ( ii ) death , either of the hypnozoite itself or the host hepatocyte ( Malato et al . , 2011 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: the model is a perfect representation
the model predicts all aspects of malaria

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The hypnozoite reservoir is predicted to be over-dispersed with many individuals having few or no hypnozoites, and some having intensely infected livers.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The model predicts that the hypnozoite reservoir is over-dispersed, meaning many individuals have few or no hypnozoites, while some have intensely infected livers.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Many infected people have few or no hypnozoites, but some have many.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The model's predictions suggest that the distribution of hypnozoites among infected individuals is 'over-dispersed'. This means that while many people might have very few or no hypnozoites, a smaller number of individuals could have a very high concentration of these dormant parasites in their livers.
allowed_evidence_spans: The hypnozoite reservoir is predicted to be over-dispersed with many individuals having few or no hypnozoites , and some having intensely infected livers .
The number of hypnozoites per individual is predicted to be over-dispersed following a negative binomial distribution .
Thus some individuals will harbour a large number of hypnozoites while some will have none .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Individuals with more hypnozoites are predicted to experience more relapses and contribute more to onwards P. vivax transmission.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The model predicts that individuals with more hypnozoites will experience more relapses and contribute more to the onward transmission of P. vivax.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: People with many hypnozoites are more likely to suffer from malaria relapses.
evidence_rows.lay_context: A key finding from the model is that individuals carrying a larger number of hypnozoites are expected to have more frequent malaria relapses. These individuals are also predicted to play a greater role in spreading P. vivax to others.
allowed_evidence_spans: Individuals with more hypnozoites are predicted to experience more relapses and contribute more to onwards P . vivax transmission .
This model predicts notable dose-dependency with increased numbers of hypnozoites associated with a greater number of relapses and shorter time to first relapse .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: all relapses are due to many hypnozoites
everyone with hypnozoites transmits the disease

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Incorporating hypnozoite killing drugs such as primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P. vivax transmission as individuals with the most hypnozoites are more likely to relapse and be targeted for treatment.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Incorporating hypnozoite-killing drugs like primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P. vivax transmission.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Adding drugs that kill hypnozoites to initial treatments may substantially reduce P. vivax transmission.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The model suggests that if drugs specifically designed to kill hypnozoites, such as primaquine, are included in standard first-line treatments for P. vivax, it could significantly reduce the overall transmission of the parasite. This is because individuals with the highest number of hypnozoites, who are most likely to relapse and seek treatment, would be targeted.
allowed_evidence_spans: Incorporating hypnozoite killing drugs such as primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P . vivax transmission as individuals with the most hypnozoites are more likely to relapse and be targeted for treatment .

The inclusion of primaquine in first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in both the P . vivax parasite rate and hypnozoite rate ( Figure 5C ) , as individuals being treated for blood-stage P . vivax infections will also have their hypnozoites removed .

A consequence of this strategy is that the hypnozoite reservoir can be targeted efficiently , as individuals with the most hypnozoites are most likely to relapse and potentially be detected by health systems .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: this is the only way to reduce transmission

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The hypnozoite reservoir can be directly targeted using drugs like primaquine, which eliminate hypnozoites from the liver.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: The hypnozoite reservoir can be directly targeted using a drug such as primaquine that can eliminate hypnozoites from the liver ( Wells et al . , 2010 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Selective logging in Amazonian forests disturbs 2 Mha annually and emits over 90 Tg of carbon to the atmosphere.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Selective logging in Amazonian forests disturbs approximately 2 million hectares annually and emits over 90 teragrams of carbon to the atmosphere.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Selective logging causes carbon loss.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Selective logging, where specific tree species are harvested, is a widespread human disturbance in tropical forests like the Amazon, leading to significant carbon emissions.
allowed_evidence_spans: When 2 Mha of Amazonian forests are disturbed by selective logging each year , more than 90 Tg of carbon ( C ) is emitted to the atmosphere .

Among those disturbances , selective logging , i . e . the selective harvest of a few merchantable tree species , is particularly widespread: in the Brazilian Amazon alone , about 2 Mha yr−1 were logged in 1999–2002 ( Asner et al . , 2005 ) .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Selective logging disturbs approximately 2 million hectares of Amazonian forests annually.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: When 2 Mha of Amazonian forests are disturbed by selective logging each year , more than 90 Tg of carbon ( C ) is emitted to the atmosphere .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Selective logging in Amazonian forests emits over 90 teragrams of carbon to the atmosphere each year.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: When 2 Mha of Amazonian forests are disturbed by selective logging each year , more than 90 Tg of carbon ( C ) is emitted to the atmosphere .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Carbon emissions from selective logging can be counterbalanced by forest regrowth.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Forest regrowth can counterbalance the carbon emissions resulting from selective logging.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Forest regrowth can compensate for carbon loss.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Unlike deforested areas, selectively logged forests often remain forested and can recover their carbon stocks as new trees grow and surviving trees continue to develop.
allowed_evidence_spans: Emissions are then counterbalanced by forest regrowth .

In contrast to deforested areas that are used for agriculture and grazing , most selectively logged forests remain as forested areas ( Asner et al . , 2006 ) and may recover C stocks ( West et al . , 2014 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study used a modeling approach, calibrated on 133 forest plots across Amazonia, to predict post-logging carbon recovery.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study utilized an original modeling approach, calibrated on a network of 133 permanent forest plots (175 ha total) across Amazonia, to provide Amazon-wide predictions of post-logging carbon recovery.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Computer modeling used to analyze data.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Researchers developed a new computer model, using data from over a hundred forest plots, to understand how factors like climate and soil affect how much carbon forests recover after logging.
allowed_evidence_spans: With an original modelling approach , calibrated on a network of 133 permanent forest plots ( 175 ha total ) across Amazonia , we link regional differences in climate , soil and initial biomass with survivors’ and recruits’ C fluxes to provide Amazon-wide predictions of post-logging C recovery .

Based on long-term ( 8–30 year ) inventory data from 13 experimentally-disturbed sites ( Sist et al . , 2015 ) across Amazonia ( Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ) , 133 permanent forest plots ( 175 ha in total ) that cover a large gradient of disturbance intensities ( ACS losses ranging from 1% to 71% ) were used to model the trajectory of those post-disturbance ACS changes ( Figure 1 ) in a comprehensive Bayesian framework .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The modeling approach was calibrated using data from 133 permanent forest plots totaling 175 hectares across Amazonia.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: With an original modelling approach , calibrated on a network of 133 permanent forest plots ( 175 ha total ) across Amazonia , we link regional differences in climate , soil and initial biomass with survivors’ and recruits’ C fluxes to provide Amazon-wide predictions of post-logging C recovery .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Net aboveground carbon recovery over 10 years is higher in the Guiana Shield and western Amazon (21 ±3 Mg C ha-1) than in the south (12 ±3 Mg C ha-1).
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Net aboveground carbon recovery over 10 years is higher in the Guiana Shield and western Amazon (21 ±3 Mg C ha-1) compared to the southern Amazon (12 ±3 Mg C ha-1), where environmental stress is high.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Carbon recovery differs between regions.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that the amount of carbon recovered after logging varies significantly by region; areas like the Guiana Shield and western Amazon recover more carbon than the southern Amazon, which experiences environmental stress like low rainfall.
allowed_evidence_spans: We show that net aboveground C recovery over 10 years is higher in the Guiana Shield and in the west ( 21 ±3 Mg C ha-1 ) than in the south ( 12 ±3 Mg C ha-1 ) where environmental stress is high ( low rainfall , high seasonality ) .
two areas , northwestern Amazonia and the Guiana Shield , with high ACS accumulation ( 21 ± 3 Mg C ha-1 over 10 year )
and one area with low ACS accumulation , southern Amazonia ( 12 ± 3 Mg C ha-1 over 10 year ) .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Environmental stress, characterized by low rainfall and high seasonality, leads to lower carbon recovery in the southern Amazon.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study highlights the key role of surviving trees in forest regrowth and provides a map of carbon recovery potential.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study highlights the key role of surviving trees in forest regrowth and elaborates a comprehensive map of post-disturbance carbon recovery potential in Amazonia.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Surviving trees play a key role.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The research emphasizes that trees that survive selective logging are crucial for the forest's ability to regrow and recover carbon, and it provides a detailed map showing where this recovery is most likely to occur.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Many decisions are thought to arise from the accumulation of noisy evidence until a certain threshold is reached.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: One theory of decision-making is that the brain simultaneously accumulates evidence for each of the options it is considering, until one option exceeds a threshold and is declared the 'winner'. This theory is known as bounded evidence accumulation.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This model suggests that the brain gathers information over time until enough evidence for one choice crosses a certain point, leading to a decision.
allowed_evidence_spans: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound .

The decision terminates when the accumulated evidence for one alternative , termed a decision variable ( DV ) , reaches a threshold or bound , thereby determining both the choice and the decision time .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy and, paradoxically, higher confidence.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The bounded evidence accumulation theory predicts that an increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically, higher confidence.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: It predicts that increasing the noisiness of the available information decreases the accuracy of decisions made in response. Counterintuitively, it also predicts that such an increase in noise speeds up decision-making and increases confidence levels.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This prediction is counterintuitive because one might expect more noise to slow down decisions and decrease confidence.
allowed_evidence_spans: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence .

The important point is that by increasing noise , the volatility manipulation accelerates the dispersion of the decision variable away from its expected value and nearer the termination bounds , hence faster RT .
Increased volatility should affect confidence because it mimics an increase in the diffusion rate .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: An increase in noise is predicted to lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and higher confidence.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: To test these predictions, we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The researchers developed a novel sensory manipulation to mimic unbiased noise in motion-selective visual cortex regions, which was verified by neuronal recordings in macaque areas MT/MST.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Using a newly developed method, the noisiness of the dot motion could be changed between trials. The effectiveness of this technique was confirmed by recording the activity of neurons in the region of the monkey brain that processes visual motion information.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This manipulation allowed them to specifically control the level of 'noise' in the visual information processed by the brain, without biasing the actual motion direction.
allowed_evidence_spans: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST .

To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST .

We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion ( RDM ) display , by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence .

We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal ( MT ) and medial superior temporal ( MST ) areas of the macaque visual cortex .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The novel sensory manipulation was verified using neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The researchers verified the desired properties of their manipulation by recording from direction-selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal ( MT ) and medial superior temporal ( MST ) areas of the macaque visual cortex .

evidence_rows.core_keep_af: In both humans and monkeys, increased noise led to faster decisions and greater confidence, with only minimal impairment to accuracy.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In both humans and monkeys, increasing the noisiness associated with the movement of the dots led to faster and more confident decision-making, just as the bounded evidence accumulation framework predicts.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This finding shows that even when the information was noisier, participants made decisions more quickly and felt more certain about them, without a significant drop in how often they were correct.

and ( iii ) showed how a framework based on the bounded accumulation of evidence can account for the joint effect of volatility on choice , reaction time and confidence .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The insulin-like signaling pathway maintains a relatively short wild-type lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by phosphorylating and inactivating DAF-16, the ortholog of the FOXO transcription factors of mammalian cells.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: How nervous systems implement the serial execution of different movements to form motor sequences is largely unknown.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The nervous system's implementation of motor sequence formation, through the serial execution of different movements, is largely unknown.

allowed_evidence_spans: Motor sequences are formed through the serial execution of different movements , but how nervous systems implement this process remains largely unknown .

Grooming consists of discrete cleaning movements that occur in predictable sequences; however , the mechanisms that govern transitions between the movements are not known ( Szebenyi , 1969; Fentress and Stilwell , 1973; Dawkins and Dawkins , 1976; Sachs , 1988 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study determined the organizational principles governing how dirty fruit flies groom their bodies with sequential movements.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The study investigated the organizational principles underlying the neural control of serial action selection in grooming.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Here , we study the organizational principles underlying the neural control of serial action selection in an innate behavior common to most limbed animals—grooming ( Sachs , 1988 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Competition experiments revealed that motor programs are organized into a suppression hierarchy, where earlier programs suppress later ones.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The motor programs for grooming in fruit flies are organized into a suppression hierarchy, where programs occurring first suppress those that occur later.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: a ‘hierarchy’ exists in the brain that exactly matches the sequence that flies normally follow
evidence_rows.lay_context: When multiple cleaning movements were triggered simultaneously, the researchers found that the movements that normally occur earlier in the grooming sequence would suppress those that occur later, forming a 'suppression hierarchy'.
allowed_evidence_spans: This enabled competition experiments revealing that the motor programs are organized into a suppression hierarchy; motor programs that occur first suppress those that occur later .

For this hypothesis to account for the fly grooming progression , the order of suppression within the hierarchy would have to match the order of the normal grooming sequence , as schematized ( Figure 3A ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Cleaning a body part reduces its sensory drive, relieving suppression of the next movement and allowing the sequence to progress.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Cleaning one body part reduces the sensory drive to its motor program, which then relieves suppression of the next movement, allowing the grooming sequence to progress down the hierarchy.
evidence_rows.lay_context: As a fly cleans a body part, the sensory input for that cleaning movement decreases. This reduction in sensory input then lifts the suppression on the next movement in the hierarchy, allowing the grooming sequence to continue.
allowed_evidence_spans: Cleaning one body part reduces the sensory drive to its motor program , which relieves suppression of the next movement , allowing the grooming sequence to progress down the hierarchy .

Once a module is selected, the reduced sensory drive that results from cleaning dust from the relevant body part gradually lowers its activation level, thereby allowing cleaning to proceed to whichever module has the next highest activation level (In Figure 4A, the removal of dust by a module is represented with blunt arrows from the winner-take-all layer to the dust).
In grooming , the active module ‘deletes’ itself from the sequence by reducing the dust stimulated sensory drive through cleaning

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: A model with independently evoked cleaning movements, activated in parallel but selected serially through hierarchical suppression, reproduced the grooming sequence.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: A model featuring independently evoked cleaning movements activated in parallel, but selected serially through hierarchical suppression, successfully reproduced the grooming sequence in fruit flies.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: computer modeling
evidence_rows.lay_context: The researchers developed a computer model where all cleaning movements are activated at the same time (in parallel) but are then chosen one by one (serially) based on the suppression hierarchy. This model accurately recreated the observed grooming sequence.
allowed_evidence_spans: A model featuring independently evoked cleaning movements activated in parallel , but selected serially through hierarchical suppression , was successful in reproducing the grooming sequence .
We next generate an empirically derived computational model that demonstrates how a suppression hierarchy can mediate the sequential selection of the cleaning motor programs .

Between the proposed models describing how nervous systems execute serial actions, hierarchical suppression through competition is a core feature of parallel response models rather than activation chain models (Houghton and Hartley, 1995; Bullock, 2004).

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This is the first example of an innate motor sequence implemented by the prevailing model for generating human action sequences.

evidence_rows.lay_context: This study is significant because it shows for the first time that an innate behavior in fruit flies uses the same organizational principles (a parallel model with hierarchical suppression) thought to be used for complex learned action sequences in humans, like typing.
allowed_evidence_spans: This provides the first example of an innate motor sequence implemented by the prevailing model for generating human action sequences .

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Previously it was reported that the TFIID complex was eliminated from cells during muscle differentiation, and that an alternative protein complex called TBP2/TAF3 recognizes and regulates the promoters of muscle-specific genes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Muscle cells develop through a process called differentiation, which involves activating specific muscle genes. It was previously thought that a protein complex called TRF3/TBP2 was essential for this activation, replacing the usual TFIID-TBP complex.
allowed_evidence_spans: Replacement of the canonical TFIID-TBP complex with TRF3/TBP2 was reported to be required for activation of muscle-gene expression .

In particular , it was recently suggested that during skeletal muscle differentiation , canonical TFIID is replaced by a complex consisting of TBP2 ( also termed TRF3 = TBP-related factor 3; gene name Tbpl2 = TATA box binding protein like 2 ) and TAF3 , which is required for activation of muscle genes ( Deato and Tjian , 2007; Deato et al . , 2008 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TBP2 is always required for muscle gene expression.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The lack of a developmental phenotype in TBP2 null mice prompted further analysis to determine whether TBP2 deficiency can compromise adult myogenesis.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The absence of a developmental phenotype in TBP2 null mice prompted further investigation into whether TBP2 deficiency affects adult myogenesis.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Previous studies showed that mice lacking TBP2 (TBP2 null mice) developed normally, suggesting TBP2 might not be crucial for muscle development. This led researchers to investigate if TBP2 is important for muscle regeneration in adults.
allowed_evidence_spans: The lack of a developmental phenotype in TBP2 null mice prompted further analysis to determine whether TBP2 deficiency can compromise adult myogenesis .

Nevertheless this hypothesis has been challenged by the observation that TBP2 null ( TBP2_KO = TBP2 knock out ) mice do not display any skeletal muscle phenotype ( Gazdag et al . , 2009 ) , indicating that TBP2 is dispensable for developmental myogenesis
To investigate the role of TBP2 in postnatal and adult skeletal myogenesis in vivo we assessed the muscle regeneration potential of TBP2 null mice ( Gazdag et al . , 2009 ) in response to injury .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TBP2 has no role in any muscle process.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: TBP2 null mice do not show any skeletal muscle phenotype, suggesting TBP2 is not essential for developmental myogenesis.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Nevertheless this hypothesis has been challenged by the observation that TBP2 null ( TBP2_KO = TBP2 knock out ) mice do not display any skeletal muscle phenotype ( Gazdag et al . , 2009 ) , indicating that TBP2 is dispensable for developmental myogenesis

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We show here that TBP2 null mice have an intact regeneration potential upon injury and that TBP2 is not expressed in established C2C12 muscle cell or in primary mouse MuSCs.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: TBP2 null mice show normal regeneration potential after injury, and TBP2 is not expressed in established C2C12 muscle cells or in primary mouse muscle stem cells (MuSCs).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Further experiments also showed that the TBP2 protein is not required for differentiation of muscle cells or for the regeneration of injured muscles, and is actually absent in muscle cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that mice without TBP2 could still regenerate muscle normally after injury. Furthermore, TBP2 was not detected in mature muscle cells (C2C12) or in the stem cells (MuSCs) that repair muscle.
allowed_evidence_spans: We show here that TBP2 null mice have an intact regeneration potential upon injury
and that TBP2 is not expressed in established C2C12 muscle cell or in primary mouse MuSCs .

Our data demonstrating the lack of requirement of TBP2 for adult skeletal muscle regeneration prompted us to compare the RNA expression profile of Tbp and Tbpl2 genes in MuSCs isolated from skeletal muscles of wild type mouse by FACS, and in the C2C12 myogenic cell line (Blau et al., 1983).
We found that TBP2 is not expressed in myotubes derived from either C2C12 myoblasts , nor from primary mouse MuSCs .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TBP2 has no function in any cell type.
TBP2 is never expressed in any muscle-related context.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: TBP2 is not expressed in myotubes derived from C2C12 myoblasts or primary mouse muscle stem cells (MuSCs).
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: We found that TBP2 is not expressed in myotubes derived from either C2C12 myoblasts , nor from primary mouse MuSCs .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: While TFIID subunits and TBP are downregulated during myoblast differentiation, reduced amounts of these proteins form a complex that is detectable on promoters of muscle genes and is essential for their expression.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: During myoblast differentiation, TFIID subunits and TBP are downregulated, but reduced amounts of these proteins still form a complex detectable on muscle gene promoters and are essential for their expression.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: However, Malecova et al. have now discovered that TFIID is actually present, albeit at reduced amounts, in differentiated muscles and that it drives the activation of muscle-specific genes during differentiation.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Despite a decrease in the levels of TFIID components and TBP during muscle cell differentiation, these proteins still form a complex. This complex is found at the regulatory regions (promoters) of muscle genes and is crucial for these genes to be expressed.
allowed_evidence_spans: While TFIID subunits and TBP are downregulated during myoblast differentiation , reduced amounts of these proteins form a complex that is detectable on promoters of muscle genes and is essential for their expression .

We observe a downregulation of mRNA expression of the TFIID subunits TBP and TAFs in myotubes derived from both C2C12s ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1A ) and from MuSCs ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1B ) , compared to undifferentiated cells ( myoblasts ) .

Indeed , TFIID subunits were detected in C2C12 nuclear extracts prepared from both proliferating myoblasts and differentiated myotubes , with a concomitant downregulation of most TFIID subunits also at the protein level ( Figure 4A ) , as previously observed ( Deato and Tjian , 2007; Zhou et al . , 2013 ) .
mRNA analysis of skeletal muscle specific genes Myog , Ckm and Acta1 demonstrates an impaired activation of the skeletal muscle program in the absence of TBP ( Figure 3D ) .
must_use_terms: detectable on promoters of muscle genes
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TFIID is completely absent during differentiation.
TBP is not involved in muscle gene expression.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: mRNA expression of TFIID subunits TBP and TAFs is downregulated in myotubes derived from both C2C12s and MuSCs compared to undifferentiated myoblasts.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: We observe a downregulation of mRNA expression of the TFIID subunits TBP and TAFs in myotubes derived from both C2C12s ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1A ) and from MuSCs ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1B ) , compared to undifferentiated cells ( myoblasts ) .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Impaired activation of the skeletal muscle program, including genes like Myog, Ckm, and Acta1, occurs in the absence of TBP.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: mRNA analysis of skeletal muscle specific genes Myog , Ckm and Acta1 demonstrates an impaired activation of the skeletal muscle program in the absence of TBP ( Figure 3D ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This evidence demonstrates that TBP2 does not replace TBP during muscle differentiation, as previously proposed, with limiting amounts of TFIID-TBP being required to promote muscle-specific gene expression.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The evidence demonstrates that TBP2 does not replace TBP during muscle differentiation, contrary to previous proposals, and that limiting amounts of TFIID-TBP are required to promote muscle-specific gene expression.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Together these efforts will allow the various aspects of gene regulation to be integrated, which will help provide a more complete understanding of the process of muscle differentiation.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This study refutes the earlier idea that TBP2 takes over from TBP during muscle differentiation. Instead, it shows that even small amounts of the TFIID-TBP complex are necessary for activating genes specific to muscle.
allowed_evidence_spans: This evidence demonstrates that TBP2 does not replace TBP during muscle differentiation , as previously proposed
with limiting amounts of TFIID-TBP being required to promote muscle-specific gene expression .
Altogether , our results are contrary to previously reported data ( Deato and Tjian , 2007 ) and demonstrate that the TFIID complex is not replaced by TBP2 upon myogenic differentiation .
This evidence firmly supports the conclusion that TBP2 does not replace TBP during muscle differentiation , as previously proposed by Deato et al . ( Deato and Tjian , 2007 ) .
must_use_terms: required to promote muscle-specific gene expression
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TBP2 has no role in muscle at all.
TFIID-TBP is the only complex involved in muscle gene expression.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The human innate immune system recognizes foreign double-stranded (ds) DNA of pathogenic origin in the intracellular environment as an essential defense mechanism.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The human innate immune system uses the ability to recognize foreign double-stranded (ds) DNA of pathogenic origin in the intracellular environment as an essential defense mechanism.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The immune system defends us from attacks by viruses, bacteria and other microbes. One way that the immune system can identify these invaders is by detecting genetic material from the microbes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The innate immune system is a crucial part of the body's defense, and it relies on detecting foreign DNA from pathogens like viruses and bacteria inside cells.
allowed_evidence_spans: The ability to recognize foreign double-stranded ( ds ) DNA of pathogenic origin in the intracellular environment is an essential defense mechanism of the human innate immune system .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The molecular mechanisms underlying the distinction between foreign DNA and host genomic material inside the nucleus are not understood.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The molecular mechanisms that distinguish between foreign DNA and host genomic material inside the nucleus are not understood.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: However, it is not clear how IFI16 and other sensor proteins are able to tell foreign and host DNA apart.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Despite the importance of this recognition, how the immune system differentiates between foreign DNA and the body's own DNA within the cell's nucleus remains a mystery.
allowed_evidence_spans: However , the molecular mechanisms underlying distinction between foreign DNA and host genomic material inside the nucleus are not understood .

The molecular mechanism by which innate immune sensors distinguish self from foreign dsDNA in the host nucleus has been a major unresolved question in innate immunology ( Kerur et al . , 2011; Unterholzner and Bowie , 2011; Li et al . , 2012; 2013; Orzalli et al . , 2012; 2013; Johnson et al . , 2014 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The nuclear innate immune sensor IFI16 one-dimensionally tracks long stretches of exposed foreign dsDNA to assemble into supramolecular signaling platforms.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The nuclear innate immune sensor IFI16 tracks long stretches of exposed foreign dsDNA one-dimensionally to assemble into supramolecular signaling platforms.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The experiments show that to start with, a few molecules of IFI16 bind to stretches of exposed foreign DNA and then move along the DNA strands. As more molecules of IFI16 bind to this DNA, they bump into each other and start to form clusters that eventually become immobile.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Using biochemical and single-molecule techniques, researchers found that the immune sensor protein IFI16 moves along long, exposed segments of foreign double-stranded DNA, forming large signaling structures.
allowed_evidence_spans: By combining biochemical assays and single-molecule techniques , we show that the nuclear innate immune sensor IFI16 one-dimensionally tracks long stretches of exposed foreign dsDNA to assemble into supramolecular signaling platforms .
Figure 2B shows that individual IFI16 molecules one-dimensionally ( 1D ) diffuse on λdsDNA while bound for several seconds .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Individual IFI16 molecules diffuse one-dimensionally (1D) on λdsDNA while bound for several seconds.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Figure 2B shows that individual IFI16 molecules one-dimensionally ( 1D ) diffuse on λdsDNA while bound for several seconds .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Nucleosomes represent barriers that prevent IFI16 from targeting host DNA by directly interfering with its one-dimensional movements.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Nucleosomes prevent IFI16 from targeting host DNA by directly interfering with its one-dimensional movements.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Further experiments show that the more tightly packed nucleosomes in host DNA molecules act as a barrier to IFI16 cluster formation because they interfere with the ability of the protein to move along the DNA.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study also found that nucleosomes, which package host DNA, act as obstacles, blocking IFI16's movement and preventing it from targeting the body's own DNA.
allowed_evidence_spans: We also demonstrate that nucleosomes represent barriers that prevent IFI16 from targeting host DNA by directly interfering with these one-dimensional movements .

These observations are consistent with the bulk experiments ( Figure 3 ) , and confirm that nucleosomes directly restrict the 1D diffusion of IFI16 and consequently limit the assembly of IFI16 signaling platforms on dsDNA .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This unique scanning-assisted assembly mechanism allows IFI16 to distinguish friend from foe and assemble into oligomers efficiently and selectively on foreign DNA.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The scanning-assisted assembly mechanism allows IFI16 to distinguish between host and foreign DNA and assemble efficiently and selectively on foreign DNA.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Stratmann, Morrone et al.’s findings show that IFI16 can only trigger immune responses when it binds to stretches of exposed DNA that are long enough to allow the assembly of IFI16 clusters.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This specific scanning and assembly process enables IFI16 to accurately differentiate between the body's own DNA and foreign DNA, ensuring it only forms clusters on foreign DNA to trigger an immune response.
allowed_evidence_spans: This unique scanning-assisted assembly mechanism allows IFI16 to distinguish friend from foe and assemble into oligomers efficiently and selectively on foreign DNA .
Second and more importantly , this assembly mechanism can only take place on foreign dsDNA and must be inhibited on host dsDNA ( Figure 1A ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Spatially targeted optical microproteomics (STOMP) is a novel proteomics technique for interrogating micron-scale regions of interest (ROIs) in mammalian tissue, with no requirement for genetic manipulation.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Spatially targeted optical microproteomics (STOMP) is a new proteomics technique that can analyze micron-scale regions of interest (ROIs) in mammalian tissue without genetic manipulation.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Hadley, Rakhit et al. have now developed a new method called spatially targeted optical microproteomics (or STOMP) that can collect proteins from small areas of cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: STOMP is a new method for studying proteins in very small, specific areas of tissue, which is useful for understanding diseases where proteins accumulate in tiny structures.
allowed_evidence_spans: Spatially targeted optical microproteomics ( STOMP ) is a novel proteomics technique for interrogating micron-scale regions of interest ( ROIs ) in mammalian tissue , with no requirement for genetic manipulation .

Spatially targeted optical microproteomics ( STOMP ) is a novel proteomics technique for interrogating micron-scale regions of interest ( ROIs ) in mammalian tissue , with no requirement for genetic manipulation .

Spatially targeted optical microproteomics ( STOMP ) is a novel proteomics technique for interrogating micron-scale regions of interest ( ROIs ) in mammalian tissue , with no requirement for genetic manipulation .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: STOMP is the only technique for this purpose.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Confocal imaging along with two photon excitation are used to covalently couple photo-tags to all proteins within each ROI, to a resolution of 0.67 µm in the xy-plane and 1.48 µm axially.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: STOMP uses confocal imaging and two-photon excitation to covalently attach photo-tags to all proteins within each region of interest (ROI).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In this method, plaques are identified under a light microscope, and their contents are attached to a molecule called a photo-affinity tag using lasers.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This process uses lasers to specifically mark proteins in the target area, allowing them to be identified later.
allowed_evidence_spans: Confocal imaging along with two photon excitation are used to covalently couple photo-tags to all proteins within each ROI , to a resolution of 0 . 67 µm in the xy-plane and 1 . 48 µm axially .

The photo-tagging procedure uses two-photon microscopy ( Skoch et al . , 2006 ) rather than conventional confocal microscopy . Two-photon microscopy can excite a small volume ( <1 µm3 , Figures 1A and Figure 2 ) anywhere in the specimen , while conventional confocal microscopy excites a continuous cone that spans the entire thickness of the specimen , which would result in the covalent attachment of the photo-tag to off-target regions .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The resolution is 0.67 µm in the xy-plane and 1.48 µm axially.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Confocal imaging along with two photon excitation are used to covalently couple photo-tags to all proteins within each ROI , to a resolution of 0 . 67 µm in the xy-plane and 1 . 48 µm axially .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: After tissue solubilization, photo-tagged proteins are isolated and identified by mass spectrometry.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: After tissue solubilization, the photo-tagged proteins are isolated and identified using mass spectrometry.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The proteins can then be identified using a well-established method called mass spectrometry.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Once marked, the proteins are extracted from the tissue and analyzed to determine their identity.
allowed_evidence_spans: After tissue solubilization , photo-tagged proteins are isolated and identified by mass spectrometry .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Mass spectrometry is the only way to identify proteins.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: As a test case, we examined amyloid plaques in an Alzheimer's disease (AD) mouse model and a post-mortem AD case, confirming known plaque constituents and discovering new ones.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: As a test case, STOMP was used to examine amyloid plaques in an Alzheimer's disease (AD) mouse model and a post-mortem AD case, confirming known plaque constituents and discovering new ones.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Hadley, Rakhit et al. used STOMP to analyze plaques present in the brains of mice that develop similar symptoms to those seen in humans with Alzheimer's disease. This revealed that these plaques contain more than 50 different proteins, some of which had not previously been found in plaques.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This application demonstrated STOMP's ability to identify proteins in disease-related structures, both confirming existing knowledge and revealing previously unknown components.
allowed_evidence_spans: As a test case , we examined amyloid plaques in an Alzheimer's disease ( AD ) mouse model and a post-mortem AD case , confirming known plaque constituents and discovering new ones .
As a test case , we examined amyloid plaques in an Alzheimer's disease ( AD ) mouse model and a post-mortem AD case , confirming known plaque constituents and discovering new ones .
Using amyloid plaques in TgCRND8 mice as a test subject, we demonstrated that STOMP is capable of determining the protein composition of pathological deposits in neurodegenerative disease.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: STOMP only works for Alzheimer's disease.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: STOMP can be applied to various biological samples including cell lines, primary cell cultures, ex vivo specimens, biopsy samples, and fixed post-mortem tissue.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: STOMP can be applied to various biological samples, including cell lines, primary cell cultures, ex vivo specimens, biopsy samples, and fixed post-mortem tissue.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: STOMP can be used to identify the proteins present in any area of a cell and thus has the potential to be widely used by scientists, not just those studying plaques.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The versatility of STOMP means it can be used in many different research settings and for various types of biological studies.
allowed_evidence_spans: STOMP can be applied to various biological samples including cell lines , primary cell cultures , ex vivo specimens , biopsy samples , and fixed post-mortem tissue .
These limitations notwithstanding, we find the STOMP technique is suitable for the analysis of formalin-fixed post-mortem human tissue.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: STOMP is the only method for these sample types.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Disruption of the Frizzled3 (Fz3) gene leads to defects in axonal growth in specific cranial and spinal motor nerves.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Disruption of the Frizzled3 (Fz3) gene causes defects in axonal growth in specific cranial motor nerves (VIIth and XIIth), the phrenic nerve, and dorsal motor nerves in fore- and hindlimbs.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Frizzled3 is involved in long-range pathfinding activity for motor neurons.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The Frizzled3 (Fz3) gene is important for the proper development of motor neuron axons, which are the 'cables' that transmit electrical signals.
allowed_evidence_spans: Disruption of the Frizzled3 ( Fz3 ) gene leads to defects in axonal growth in the VIIth and XIIth cranial motor nerves , the phrenic nerve , and the dorsal motor nerve in fore- and hindlimbs .
Using conventional and conditional loss-of-function alleles for Fz3 , we show that Fz3 is required for a subset of cranial and spinal motor axons to grow to their peripheral targets .

In E11 . 5-E13 . 5 Fz3−/− embryos anti-NF immunostaining revealed a thinning of the XIIth ( hypoglossal ) nerve ( Figure 1B , B′ ) , the phrenic nerve ( Figure 1C , C′ ) , and the dorsal nerves of the fore- and hindlimbs ( described more fully below ) .
must_use_terms: VIIth and XIIth cranial motor nerves

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The motor neuron phenotypes observed in Fz3−/− mice include defects in the VIIth cranial nerve, XIIth cranial nerve, phrenic nerve, and dorsal nerves innervating the limbs.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Olig2Cre/+;Fz3CKO/− mice exhibit the complete spectrum of motor neuron phenotypes shown by Fz3−/− mice: (1) VIIth nerve axons do not form the well-defined C-shaped tract looping around the VIth cranial nerve nucleus; (2) the XIIth cranial nerve is markedly thinned and fails to innervate the tongue at E13.5; (3) the phrenic nerve is thinned; and (4) the dorsal nerves innervating the fore- and hindlimbs are thinned.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: In Fz3−/− limbs, dorsal axons stall at a precise location in the nerve plexus and do not reroute to other trajectories.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: In Fz3-deficient limbs, dorsal axons stop at a specific location in the nerve plexus and do not reroute to other paths.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In mutant animals, many motor axons failed to form connections with their targets, stalling midway.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Unlike other axon path-finding mutants, Fz3-deficient axons do not find alternative routes; they simply stop growing.
allowed_evidence_spans: In Fz3−/− limbs , dorsal axons stall at a precise location in the nerve plexus , and , in contrast to the phenotypes of several other axon path-finding mutants , Fz3−/− dorsal axons do not reroute to other trajectories .

More specifically, in Fz3−/− limbs an abrupt decrease in diameter is observed in the dorsal nerve immediately distal to the emergence of its first major side branch (Figure 4B′–H′, M). Therefore, the defect in the Fz3−/− limb appears to be a stalling of LMCL axons at this location.

the ventral nerve exhibits a small decrease in thickness in 5/6 comparisons, with 4/6 showing a difference that is statistically significant (p<0.05), implying that dorsal nerve axons have not rerouted to the ventral nerve, which would have then shown an increase in thickness;

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The defect in Fz3−/− limbs appears to be a stalling of LMCL axons immediately distal to the emergence of the dorsal nerve's first major side branch.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: More specifically, in Fz3−/− limbs an abrupt decrease in diameter is observed in the dorsal nerve immediately distal to the emergence of its first major side branch (Figure 4B′–H′, M). Therefore, the defect in the Fz3−/− limb appears to be a stalling of LMCL axons at this location.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Affected motor neurons undergo cell death 2 days prior to the normal wave of developmental cell death.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Affected motor neurons in Fz3-deficient organisms die two days before the normal developmental cell death wave that occurs when muscles are innervated.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The neurons from which stalled axons originated died soon afterwards.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This premature cell death suggests that neurons need their axons to reach intermediate targets on schedule to receive survival signals.
allowed_evidence_spans: Affected motor neurons undergo cell death 2 days prior to the normal wave of developmental cell death that coincides with innervation of muscle targets , providing in vivo evidence for the idea that developing neurons with long-range axons are programmed to die unless their axons arrive at intermediate targets on schedule .

Affected cranial and spinal motor neurons die shortly after their axons stall , providing in vivo evidence for the general idea that as growing axons arrive at intermediate targets essential survival signals are relayed to their cell bodies .
Thus, in Fz3−/− embryos a discrete subset of motor neurons exhibits both axon growth defects and apoptotic cell death at E11.5-E12.5.
must_use_terms: normal wave of developmental cell death

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Precocious motor neuron death occurs in the VIIth and XIIth cranial nerve nuclei in Fz3−/− embryos at E12.5.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Similarly, in the VIIth and XIIth cranial nerve nuclei at E12.5, there is an analogous wave of precocious motor neuron death that is not observed in Fz3+/− controls (Figure 5H–K′).

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: These experiments implicate planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling in motor axon growth.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: These experiments suggest that planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling is involved in motor axon growth.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The work provides new insights into molecular mechanisms by which connections are established.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling is a process typically known for organizing cells in flat tissues, but this study suggests it also plays a role in guiding axon growth.
allowed_evidence_spans: These experiments implicate planar cell polarity ( PCP ) signaling in motor axon growth and they highlight the question of how PCP proteins , which form cell–cell complexes in epithelia , function in the dynamic context of axonal growth .

Fz3 appears to be part of a system that provides directional information to growing axons , as indicated by the observation that in Fz3−/− embryos commissural sensory axons in the spinal cord orient randomly instead of turning rostrally after midline crossing ( Lyuksyutova et al . , 2003 ) .

While current models of PCP protein action in growth cones are necessarily speculative , the axon growth phenotypes suggest that the signaling repertoire of PCP proteins is more diverse than would be predicted from considerations based only on epithelia .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The study raises the question of how PCP proteins, which form cell-cell complexes in epithelia, function in the dynamic process of axonal growth.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: These experiments implicate planar cell polarity ( PCP ) signaling in motor axon growth and they highlight the question of how PCP proteins , which form cell–cell complexes in epithelia , function in the dynamic context of axonal growth .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Transposable elements (TEs) are thought to have helped establish gene regulatory networks.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Transposable elements (TEs) are believed to have contributed to the establishment of gene regulatory networks.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Transposable elements can be 'domesticated' and used to the host's advantage, for example, by regulating other genes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Transposable elements are repetitive sequences that make up a significant portion of the genome and are thought to play a role in how genes are controlled.
allowed_evidence_spans: Transposable elements ( TEs ) are thought to have helped establish gene regulatory networks .
On the other , TEs can be co-opted ( or exapted ) by the host to serve gene regulatory roles , such as alternative promoters or enhancers ( Chuong et al . , 2017 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TEs always establish gene regulatory networks
TEs are the only factor in gene regulation

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Both embryonic and extraembryonic lineages of the early mouse embryo have seemingly co-opted TEs as enhancers, but there is little evidence that they play significant roles in gene regulation.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: There is limited evidence that transposable elements (TEs) play significant roles in gene regulation, despite being co-opted as enhancers in early mouse embryo lineages.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: It remains unclear to what extent transposable elements have shaped genome regulation throughout evolution.
evidence_rows.lay_context: While transposable elements appear to act as enhancers (which boost gene activity) in early mouse embryo development, their actual importance in gene regulation is not well-established.
allowed_evidence_spans: Both the embryonic and extraembryonic lineages of the early mouse embryo have seemingly co-opted TEs as enhancers , but there is little evidence that they play significant roles in gene regulation .
However , it remains unclear to what extent such lineage-specific TEs are important for maintaining gene expression programmes during preimplantation development .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TEs are not important for gene regulation

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Here we tested a set of long terminal repeat TE families for roles as enhancers in mouse embryonic and trophoblast stem cells.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study tested a set of long terminal repeat (LTR) transposable element (TE) families for their roles as enhancers in mouse embryonic and trophoblast stem cells.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Todd et al. investigate whether particular transposable elements, suspected to boost gene activity, are essential for normal gene expression in early mouse development.
evidence_rows.lay_context: To address this, researchers specifically investigated certain families of transposable elements, called long terminal repeat (LTR) TEs, in mouse embryonic and trophoblast stem cells to see if they function as enhancers.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here we tested a set of long terminal repeat TE families for roles as enhancers in mouse embryonic and trophoblast stem cells .

Here we have tested the gene regulatory function of specific TE families in ESCs and TSCs using genetic and epigenetic editing approaches , and compared them with predictions from extensive analyses of epigenomic and transcriptomic data .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TEs were tested in all cell types

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The study used genetic and epigenetic editing to test the gene regulatory function of specific transposable element (TE) families.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Here we have tested the gene regulatory function of specific TE families in ESCs and TSCs using genetic and epigenetic editing approaches , and compared them with predictions from extensive analyses of epigenomic and transcriptomic data .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Epigenomic and transcriptomic data suggested that a large number of TEs helped to establish tissue-specific gene expression programmes.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Epigenomic and transcriptomic data suggested that many transposable elements (TEs) helped establish tissue-specific gene expression programs.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: One idea is that the spread of transposable elements can help to establish large regulatory networks.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Initial analyses of epigenomic and transcriptomic data indicated that a substantial number of TEs might be involved in creating gene expression patterns specific to different tissues.
allowed_evidence_spans: Epigenomic and transcriptomic data suggested that a large number of TEs helped to establish tissue-specific gene expression programmes .

Primarily based on epigenomic data , evidence to date suggests that particular TE families have contributed to the evolution of tissue-specific gene regulatory networks in contexts such as early development ( Kunarso et al . , 2010 ) , placentation ( Chuong et al . , 2013 ) , pregnancy ( Lynch et al . , 2011 ) and innate immunity ( Chuong et al . , 2016 ) , amongst others .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: TEs are the only cause of tissue-specific gene expression
All TEs establish gene expression programs

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Membrane nanodomains have been implicated in Ras signaling, but their nature and interaction with Ras remain obscure.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The nature of membrane nanodomains and their interaction with Ras signaling are not well understood.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: It has been suggested that to prevent these signals from being accidently activated, Ras molecules must group together at specialized sites within the membrane before passing on their message. evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This revealed that Ras molecules quickly diffuse along the inside of the membrane until they arrive at certain locations that cause them to halt. However, computer models consisting of just the ‘fast’ and ‘immobile’ state could not correctly re-capture the way Ras molecules moved along the membrane. Lee et al. found that for these models to mimic the movement of Ras, a third ‘intermediate’ state of Ras mobility needed to be included. To investigate this further, Lee et al. created a fluorescent map that overlaid all the individual paths taken by each Ras molecule. The map showed regions in the membrane where the Ras molecules had stopped and possibly clustered together. Each of these ‘immobilization domains’ were then surrounded by an ‘intermediate domain’ where Ras molecules had begun to slow down their movement.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that KRasG12D moves in three distinct ways on the membrane: it can diffuse quickly across most of the membrane, move at an intermediate speed within larger domains (about 200 nm), or become immobile within smaller domains (about 70 nm) that are nested inside the intermediate domains.

Several potential mechanisms have been proposed: 1 ) an inverse gradient of BMP antagonists imparts the shape of the BMP signaling gradient ( Figure 1C ) ( Blitz et al . , 2000; Connors et al . , 1999; Little and Mullins , 2006; Thomsen , 1997 ) , 2 ) BMP antagonists generate the peak BMP signaling levels by shuttling BMP ligand to these regions ( Figure 1B , D ) ( Ben-Zvi et al . , 2008; Shilo et al . , 2013; Zhang et al . , 2007 )

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Maintaining the essential functions of mitochondria requires mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Mitochondria need mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins to maintain their essential functions.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Proteins are molecules that need to fold into the right shape to do their job. If proteins lose that shape, not only do they stop working but they risk clumping together and becoming toxic, potentially leading to disease.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Mitochondria, which provide cells with energy, require mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins to maintain their essential functions.
allowed_evidence_spans: Maintaining the essential functions of mitochondria requires mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This study established temperature-sensitive (ts-) peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane (MOM) proteins as novel model QC substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study established temperature-sensitive (ts-) peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane (MOM) proteins as new model quality control substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: To do this, they used baker’s yeast, a model laboratory organism that shares many fundamental properties with animal cells, but which is easier to manipulate genetically. evidence_rows.lay_context: To investigate these pathways, researchers used baker's yeast and created temperature-sensitive proteins on the mitochondrial outer membrane that would misfold when the temperature increased, acting as model substrates for quality control.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here , we establish temperature-sensitive ( ts- ) peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane ( MOM ) proteins as novel model QC substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae .

While previous mitochondrial UPS substrates have consisted primarily of native proteins ( Belgareh-Touzé et al . , 2017; Cohen et al . , 2008; Heo et al . , 2010; Wu et al . , 2016 ) , sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts contain mutations that render them unstable at the non-permissive temperature , and thus mimic damaged , misfolded proteins.

The ts- nature of these substrates, coupled with their tight association with the MOM, enabled study of their mitochondrial degradation without concerns of mislocalization to the cytosol or elsewhere.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We identify CD44 expression as a sensitive reporter of tonic mTOR-S6 kinase signaling through a novel mouse strain, chino, with a reduction-of-function mutation in Mtor.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: CD44 expression is a sensitive reporter of tonic mTOR-S6 kinase signaling, identified using a novel mouse strain, chino, with a reduction-of-function mutation in Mtor.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The origins of the T helper cells were traced to excessive activity on a signaling pathway that involves a protein called mTOR.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This finding establishes CD44 as a useful indicator for the activity of the mTOR signaling pathway, which is crucial for cell growth and metabolism, and can be implicated in immune dysregulation.
allowed_evidence_spans: We identify CD44 expression as a sensitive reporter of tonic mTOR-S6 kinase signaling through a novel mouse strain , chino , with a reduction-of-function mutation in Mtor .
demonstrating that CD44 expression is a highly sensitive reporter of small changes in basal mTOR activity in CD4+ T cells .

T-cell CD44 expression is also sensitive to mTOR activity , being reduced by the partial loss-of-function Mtorchino ( Figure 8 ) and Mtortm1Lgm ( Zhang et al . , 2011 ) alleles , and dramatically decreased in the absence of Rictor ( Delgoffe et al . , 2011 ) , a binding partner of mTOR .

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Excessive activity on a signaling pathway that involves a protein called mTOR.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This finding links the Rasgrp1Anaef mutation to increased activity in the mTOR pathway, which is known to regulate cell growth and proliferation, suggesting a potential mechanism for the observed immune dysregulation.
allowed_evidence_spans: Elevated tonic mTOR-S6 signaling occurs in Rasgrp1Anaef naïve CD4+ T cells .
In contrast to Rasgrp1 deletion , the Rasgrp1Anaef missense variant increases tonic mTOR signaling in naïve CD4+ T cells .
These data reveal constitutively increased expression of two reporters of mTOR activity in Rasgrp1Anaef naïve CD4+ T cells: the well-established reporter P-S6 and the reporter clarified here , CD44 .
