Genetic reduction of mTOR function in Rasgrp1Anaef mice normalizes CD44 expression on naïve CD4+ T cells and abolishes excessive accumulation of effector T cells and autoantibodies , demonstrating a central role for increased mTOR activity in driving immune dysregulation in Rasgrp1Anaef mice .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Mutations in SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family members are common in cancer, but their mechanisms in tumorigenesis are poorly understood.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Mutations in members of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family are common in cancer, but the mechanisms by which disruption of SWI/SNF components alters tumorigenesis are poorly understood.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Around 25% of pancreatic cancers contain mutations in genes that produce proteins of the SWI/SNF complex.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The SWI/SNF complex is a group of proteins that reorganize chromatin, which is how DNA is packed in cells. This reorganization affects which genes can be activated.
allowed_evidence_spans: Mutations in members of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family are common events in cancer
but the mechanisms whereby disruption of SWI/SNF components alters tumorigenesis remain poorly understood .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: To study pancreatic cancer initiation, researchers used a mouse model with inducible and reversible suppression of Arid1a, a SWI/SNF subunit, in the presence of oncogenic KrasG12D.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study modeled the effect of loss-of-function mutations in the SWI/SNF subunit Arid1a in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) initiation using shRNA-triggered, inducible, and reversible suppression of Arid1a in the mouse pancreas with oncogenic KrasG12D.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Livshits et al. have now genetically engineered mice to investigate how one such SWI/SNF complex protein, called Arid1a, affects how pancreatic cancer develops using a genetic approach that made possible to temporarily halt the production of Arid1a in acinar cells by feeding these mice an antibiotic.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Arid1a is a specific protein within the SWI/SNF complex. The researchers used a method to temporarily turn off Arid1a production in mouse pancreatic cells, which also had an over-activated Kras gene, known to promote cancer.
allowed_evidence_spans: To model the effect of loss of function mutations in the SWI/SNF subunit Arid1a in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma ( PDAC ) initiation , we directed shRNA triggered , inducible and reversible suppression of Arid1a to the mouse pancreas in the setting of oncogenic KrasG12D .

In this study , we used a rapid and robust mouse-modeling platform to study the consequences of inducible and reversible suppression of the Arid1a SWI/SNF subunit in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The study used shRNA-triggered suppression.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: shRNA triggered

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: In the adult pancreas, postnatal silencing of Arid1a with sustained KrasG12D expression rapidly and irreversibly reprogrammed acinar cells into mucinous PDAC precursor lesions.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Arid1a cooperates with Kras in the adult pancreas, as postnatal silencing of Arid1a following sustained KrasG12D expression induces rapid and irreversible reprogramming of acinar cells into mucinous PDAC precursor lesions.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Within just two weeks of stopping the production of Arid1a, the acinar cells stopped producing digestive enzymes and started making other proteins that are typically found in cancerous cells, indicating that Arid1a is involved in maintaining the normal identity and activity of these cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Acinar cells are a type of pancreatic cell. When Arid1a was turned off in adult mice that also had active Kras, these acinar cells quickly changed their identity and became early-stage cancerous lesions, and this change could not be reversed.
allowed_evidence_spans: Arid1a cooperates with Kras in the adult pancreas
as postnatal silencing of Arid1a following sustained KrasG12D expression induces rapid and irreversible reprogramming of acinar cells into mucinous PDAC precursor lesions .

Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous , pancreatic cancer precursor lesions that cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The reprogramming was rapid.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: rapid

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The reprogramming was irreversible.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: In contrast, Arid1a silencing during embryogenesis, concurrent with KrasG12D activation, led to the retention of acinar cell fate.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Arid1a silencing during embryogenesis, concurrent with KrasG12D activation, leads to retention of acinar cell fate in mice.
evidence_rows.lay_context: However, if Arid1a was turned off much earlier, during the embryonic development of the mice, and at the same time Kras was activated, the acinar cells surprisingly kept their normal identity instead of changing into cancerous precursors.
allowed_evidence_spans: In contrast , Arid1a silencing during embryogenesis , concurrent with KrasG12D activation , leads to retention of acinar cell fate .
whereas , when occurring concomitant with KrasG12D activation , it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype ( E7 cohort ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: These results demonstrate Arid1a as a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity and highlight the unanticipated influence of timing and genetic context on SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Arid1a is a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity, and the timing and genetic context have an unanticipated influence on the effects of SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The results presented by Livshits et al. provide the first evidence of how alterations to Arid1a can lead to irreversible changes in the identity and activity of pancreatic acinar cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The findings show that Arid1a plays a key role in controlling how acinar cells change in response to Kras. The timing of when Arid1a is disrupted and the specific genetic environment significantly impact how SWI/SNF complex changes affect cancer development in epithelial tissues.
allowed_evidence_spans: Together , our results demonstrate Arid1a as a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity
and underscore an unanticipated influence of timing and genetic context on the effects of SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis .
these observations indicate that the timing of SWI/SNF perturbation can have a dramatic effect on tumorigenesis phenotypes .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: SWI/SNF alterations always lead to the same outcome

To quantitatively assess sporozoite motility over the first 120 min after inoculation into the skin of a mouse , we generated P . berghei sporozoites expressing the fluorescent protein mCherry under the control of a strong sporozoite-stage promoter ( Figure 1—figure supplement 3 ) and visualized them in the ear pinna .
Sporozoites were injected intradermally into the ear pinna of C57BL/6 mice for imaging.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Our data suggest that sporozoites exhibit two types of motility: in regions far from blood vessels, they exhibit 'avascular motility', defined by high speed and less confinement, while in the vicinity of blood vessels their motility is more constrained.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Plasmodium sporozoites exhibit two types of motility: 'avascular motility' (high speed, less confinement) in regions far from blood vessels and more constrained motility near blood vessels.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This revealed that the parasites have two ways of moving. After first being injected, the parasites move quickly and freely. The parasites slow down when they come close to a blood vessel and move on or around the vessel for some time before entering it.
evidence_rows.lay_context: When sporozoites are near blood vessels, their gliding speed decreases, and their movement becomes more confined compared to their faster, less confined movement in areas away from vessels.

and suggest that sporozoites in the dermis exhibit two types of motility: ‘avascular motility’, which is defined by high speed and less confinement, leading to maximal displacements in avascular areas and a more constrained ‘perivascular motility’, which is observed once the parasite glides in proximity of a blood vessel.
Apparent speed, with lines representing mean values, reveals a decrease in gliding speed once sporozoites are in proximity of blood vessels.

the majority of sporozoite tracks that overlap with blood vessels describe trajectories that have a curvature of 0.125–0.2 μm−1, which, remarkably, equals the curvature of the circumference of dermal capillaries (Figure 2D)

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Imaging of sporozoites with mutations in key adhesive proteins highlight the importance of the sporozoite's gliding speed and its ability to modulate adhesive properties for successful exit from the inoculation site.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Imaging sporozoites with mutations in key adhesive proteins showed the importance of gliding speed and the ability to modulate adhesive properties for successful exit from the inoculation site.

The sporozoite's ability to regulate its adhesive interactions is a key factor for successful movement through and out of the dermis.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Mutant sporozoites with altered gliding speed or adhesive properties showed significantly reduced ability to invade blood vessels and exit the inoculation site, indicating these factors are crucial for infection.

The importance of high sporozoite gliding speed is highlighted by the behavior of the TRAP-VAL mutant that moves with less than half the motile speed of wild-type control parasites in the dermis . This decrease in speed corresponds to the reduction of final MSD , which reduces the area of tissue explored by 70% . Consequently , TRAP-VAL sporozoites have a significantly decreased chance to encounter and invade a blood vessel , which together with the increase in number of non-motile TRAP-VAL sporozoites , largely explains their reduced infectivity ( Ejigiri et al . , 2012 ) .

Our data with both TRAP-VAL and CSΔN mutant sporozoites demonstrate that the sporozoite's ability to regulate its adhesive intereactions is a key factor for successful movement through and out of the dermis.
Mutant sporozoites that display modest changes in motility pattern or speed have dramatic decreases in blood vessel invasion and infectivity .

allowed_evidence_spans: We also demonstrate a strong selection for the avoidance of stochastic mRNA:ncRNA interactions across prokaryotes , and that these have a greater impact on protein abundance than mRNA structure or codon usage .

Here we show that crosstalk interactions between ncRNAs and mRNAs also impact protein abundance , and that such interactions have a greater effect than either mRNA secondary structure or codon usage .

To examine if avoidance of stochastic mRNA:ncRNA interactions is a feature of transcriptomes in bacteria and archaea , we estimated the strength of all possible intermolecular RNA interactions using a minimum free energy ( MFE ) model ( Mückstein et al . , 2006 ) using core ncRNAs and mRNAs .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: For 97% of species studied, there is a reduced capacity for interaction between native RNAs relative to controls.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: For 97% of species , we find a reduced capacity for interaction between native RNAs relative to controls .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: By generating synonymously variant green fluorescent protein (GFP) mRNAs with different potential for mRNA:ncRNA interactions, we demonstrate that GFP levels correlate well with interaction avoidance.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: GFP levels correlate well with interaction avoidance when synonymously variant green fluorescent protein (GFP) mRNAs with different potential for mRNA:ncRNA interactions are generated.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Those messengers that were designed to avoid interacting with other RNAs yielded far more protein than those that were not.
evidence_rows.lay_context: To test this, the researchers created different versions of green fluorescent protein (GFP) mRNA that varied only in their ability to avoid ncRNA interactions. They found that higher avoidance led to higher GFP protein levels.
allowed_evidence_spans: By generating synonymously variant green fluorescent protein ( GFP ) mRNAs with different potential for mRNA:ncRNA interactions , we demonstrate that GFP levels correlate well with interaction avoidance .
Optimal and high avoidance GFP mRNAs produce the highest expression while low avoidance GFP mRNAs have the lowest expression ( p=1 . 35 × 10−5 , Kruskal-Wallis test ) .
We use a set of GFP mRNA constructs that all maintain the same G+C content , codon adaptation index ( CAI ) and internal secondary structure but host either very high or very low avoidance values .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The avoidance model showed the highest and most significant correlation with GFP expression in the dataset (Rs = 0.65, p=1.69 × 10−20).
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Our avoidance model showed the highest and most significant correlation with GFP expression in that dataset ( Rs = 0 . 65 , p=1 . 69 × 10−20 ) ( Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D , E , F ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Therefore, taking stochastic mRNA:ncRNA interactions into account enables precise modulation of protein abundance.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Taking stochastic mRNA:ncRNA interactions into account enables precise modulation of protein abundance.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The findings show that taking this kind of avoidance into account can improve predictions about how much protein will be produced and should therefore make it easier to control protein production in experimental systems.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This means that by considering and manipulating how mRNA avoids random interactions with ncRNA, scientists can precisely control the amount of protein produced.
allowed_evidence_spans: Therefore , taking stochastic mRNA:ncRNA interactions into account enables precise modulation of protein abundance .
Applying this knowledge to mRNA design will enable precise control of protein abundance through the incorporation or exclusion of inhibitory interactions with native ncRNAs .
We therefore predict that taking crosstalk into account will enable the design of constructs where protein expression levels can be precisely controlled .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: It remains unclear whether the denervation of neuromuscular junctions (NMJ) in ALS is simply the first manifestation of a globally degenerating motor neuron.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: It remains unclear whether the denervation of neuromuscular junctions (NMJ) in ALS is simply the first manifestation of a globally degenerating motor neuron or arises from local branch-specific degeneration.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Does a motoneuron lose all of its connections with muscle fibers at once, or do the connections break down a few at a time?
evidence_rows.lay_context: The loss of neuromuscular junctions (NMJs), which are connections between motor neurons and muscles, is an early event in ALS, but the exact pattern of this denervation is not fully understood.
allowed_evidence_spans: Despite being an early event in ALS , it remains unclear whether the denervation of neuromuscular junctions ( NMJ ) is simply the first manifestation of a globally degenerating motor neuron . However , whether early NMJ denervation arises from local branch-specific degeneration ( ‘dying-back hypothesis’ ) or is merely the manifestation of a diseased and globally degenerating motor neuron remains ill-defined .

Denervation of NMJs is observed prior to symptom onset ( Clark et al . , 2016; Fischer et al . , 2004; Pun et al . , 2006; Tallon et al . , 2016; Vinsant et al . , 2013 ) and before any significant MN axonal or cell body loss ( Fischer et al . , 2004; Vinsant et al . , 2013 ) .

Loss of neuromuscular junctions ( NMJs ) is a key pathological event in ALS patients ( Fischer et al . , 2004; Killian et al . , 1994 ) and in animal models of the disease ( Clark et al . , 2016; Fischer et al . , 2004; Frey et al . , 2000; Pun et al . , 2006; Tallon et al . , 2016 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: ALS always starts with global motor neuron degeneration.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Using in vivo imaging of single axons and their NMJs over a three-month period, we identify that single motor-units are dismantled asynchronously in SOD1G37R mice.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study used in vivo imaging of single axons and their neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) over a three-month period in SOD1G37R mice and found that single motor-units are dismantled asynchronously.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Martineau et al. found that individual neurons lose their connections to muscle fibers gradually.
evidence_rows.lay_context: To investigate this, researchers used a mouse model of ALS (SOD1G37R mice) and tracked individual motor units over three months.

Cg-Tg ( Thy1-YFP ) HJrs/J]; The Jackson laboratories , Bar Harbor , ME , stock number 003782 ) ( Feng et al . , 2000 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: All motor units are dismantled at the same time.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Weeks prior to complete axonal degeneration, the dismantling of axonal branches is accompanied by contemporaneous new axonal sprouting resulting in synapse formation onto nearby NMJs.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Weeks prior to complete axonal degeneration, the dismantling of axonal branches is accompanied by contemporaneous new axonal sprouting, resulting in synapse formation onto nearby NMJs.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Motoneurons grow new branches and form new connections even while losing their old ones.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that before an entire axon degenerates, individual branches are dismantled, but new branches also sprout and form new connections.
allowed_evidence_spans: We reveal that weeks prior to complete axonal degeneration , the dismantling of axonal branches is accompanied by contemporaneous new axonal sprouting resulting in synapse formation onto nearby NMJs .

Importantly , we found that over half of analyzed MUs both lost and formed new NMJs throughout the imaging process ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1 , 13/19 arbors , 8/11 animals ) , showing that these opposite processes can occur simultaneously within a single MU .

Surprisingly , a vast majority of MUs in SOD1G37R/YFP also sprouted toward nearby nAChR-rich postsynaptic sites , forming new synaptic contacts on muscle fibers that they did not innervate initially ( MU expansions or ‘heterologous re-innervation’ , Figure 4A , B; 76/253 NMJs , 14/19 arbors , 9/11 animals ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Axonal degeneration is always sudden and complete.
New innervation never occurs in ALS.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Over half of analyzed motor units (MUs) both lost and formed new neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) simultaneously throughout the imaging process.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Importantly , we found that over half of analyzed MUs both lost and formed new NMJs throughout the imaging process ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1 , 13/19 arbors , 8/11 animals ) , showing that these opposite processes can occur simultaneously within a single MU .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Denervation events tend to propagate from the first lost NMJ, consistent with a contribution of neuromuscular factors extrinsic to motor neurons, with distal branches being more susceptible.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Denervation events tend to propagate from the first lost NMJ, with distal branches being more susceptible, suggesting a contribution of neuromuscular factors extrinsic to motor neurons.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This denervation process tends to spread from the initial lost connection, and the branches furthest from the motor neuron cell body are more vulnerable.
allowed_evidence_spans: Denervation events tend to propagate from the first lost NMJ , consistent with a contribution of neuromuscular factors extrinsic to motor neurons , with distal branches being more susceptible .

Indeed , NMJs arising from distal axonal branches were more susceptible to being lost ( Figure 4D , red dots , 38 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 010 ) , while MU expansions were more likely to occur on proximal branches ( mainly first-order branches ) ( Figure 4D , blue dots , 76 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 001 ) .

These results unravel a propagation pattern and suggest that factors extrinsic to motor axons ( i . e . the local neuromuscular environment ) interact with the intrinsic properties of motor axons ( e . g . susceptibility of specific branches ) , to shape the pattern of NMJ loss in ALS .
must_use_terms: neuromuscular factors extrinsic to motor neurons
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Only intrinsic motor neuron factors cause denervation.
All branches are equally susceptible to denervation.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) arising from distal axonal branches were more susceptible to being lost.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Indeed , NMJs arising from distal axonal branches were more susceptible to being lost ( Figure 4D , red dots , 38 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 010 ) , while MU expansions were more likely to occur on proximal branches ( mainly first-order branches ) ( Figure 4D , blue dots , 76 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 001 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: These results show that NMJ denervation in ALS is a complex and dynamic process of continuous denervation and new innervation rather than a manifestation of sudden global motor neuron degeneration.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The results show that NMJ denervation in ALS is a complex and dynamic process of continuous denervation and new innervation, rather than a manifestation of sudden global motor neuron degeneration.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This dual process of pruning and budding lasts for several weeks, until eventually the motoneuron dies.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This indicates that NMJ denervation in ALS is a dynamic process involving both loss and formation of new connections, not a sudden, widespread motor neuron failure.
allowed_evidence_spans: These results show that NMJ denervation in ALS is a complex and dynamic process of continuous denervation and new innervation rather than a manifestation of sudden global motor neuron degeneration .

Altogether , these results show that rather than being exclusively degenerating or compensating , MUs are highly dynamic during disease progression , with specific branches either expanding or disassembling .
Strikingly , most MUs in SOD1 mutant mice ( 16/19 arbors , 10/11 animals ) behaved in a similar fashion , that is , losing NMJs over several imaging sessions rather than abruptly .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: ALS denervation is always sudden and global.
There is no new innervation in ALS.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Adjuvant tamoxifen therapy improves survival in breast cancer patients.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Adjuvant tamoxifen therapy improves survival in breast cancer patients.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The drug tamoxifen blocks estrogen receptors, stopping cells from responding to the hormone. As such, it is often used to reduce the likelihood that estrogen-dependent breast cancer will come back after treatment.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Tamoxifen is a common treatment for hormone-responsive breast cancer.
allowed_evidence_spans: Adjuvant tamoxifen therapy improves survival in breast cancer patients .

This exceptionally effective therapy remains standard of care for people with hormone-responsive cancers , and reduction of recurrence persists for at least 10 years of continuous tamoxifen treatment ( Davies et al . , 2013; Chlebowski et al . , 2014; Gierach et al . , 2017 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Long-term tamoxifen treatment causes side effects that impact health and quality of life, including hot flashes, changes in bone density, and fatigue.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Long-term tamoxifen treatment causes side effects that impact health and quality of life, including hot flashes, changes in bone density, and fatigue.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: However, its use can induce hot flashes, changes in bone density, fatigue and other life-altering side effects.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Despite its benefits, long-term tamoxifen treatment can lead to negative side effects.
allowed_evidence_spans: Unfortunately , long-term treatment comes with side effects that impact health and quality of life , including hot flashes , changes in bone density , and fatigue .

In contrast to these benefits , tamoxifen therapy has been associated with a variety of negative side effects , including increased risk for hot flashes ( Love et al . , 1991; Howell et al . , 2005; Francis et al . , 2015 ) , endometrial cancer and venous thromboembolic events ( Fisher et al . , 1998; Cuzick et al . , 2007 ) , bone loss ( Powles et al . , 1996 ) , and fatigue ( Haghighat et al . , 2003 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The specific tissues and cells that mediate the negative side effects of tamoxifen are unclear, partly due to a lack of proven animal models.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The specific tissues and cells that mediate the negative side effects of tamoxifen are unclear, partly due to a lack of proven animal models.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Understanding the biological basis of these side effects has been challenging due to the absence of suitable animal models.
allowed_evidence_spans: Partly due to a lack of proven animal models , the tissues and cells that mediate these negative side effects are unclear .
Here , we take the first steps to define the cell types and cellular mechanisms that mediate some of the undesirable side effects experienced by people undergoing tamoxifen therapy .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Mice undergoing tamoxifen treatment experience changes in temperature, bone, and movement.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Mice undergoing tamoxifen treatment experience changes in temperature, bone, and movement.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: When the rodents were given tamoxifen for 28 days, they experienced changes in temperature, bone density and movement similar to those found in humans.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study established a mouse model where tamoxifen treatment replicated some of the physiological changes seen in humans.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here , we show that mice undergoing tamoxifen treatment experience changes in temperature , bone , and movement .

These effects are similar to those experienced by people receiving tamoxifen therapy , who experience hot flashes , lethargy , and changes in bone density , among other symptoms ( Love et al . , 1991; Powles et al . , 1996; Fisher et al . , 1998; Loprinzi et al . , 2000; Haghighat et al . , 2003; Howell et al . , 2005; Kligman and Younus , 2010; Francis et al . , 2015 ) .

We demonstrate the utility of mice as a good model to study many of tamoxifen’s physiological effects; tamoxifen administration in mice increases heat dissipation , decreases movement , and increases bone density .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Tamoxifen-treated mice showed significantly lower core body temperature compared to controls.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Similarly , tamoxifen-treated mice showed significantly lower core body temperature compared to controls, as indicated by 24 hr averages from the last week of treatment ( Sidak's Post-hoc: 24 hr p=0 . 0076 , see Supplementary file 2 for detailed statistics ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that tamoxifen treatment induces widespread gene expression changes in the hypothalamus and preoptic area (hypothalamus-POA).
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Tamoxifen treatment induces widespread gene expression changes in the hypothalamus and preoptic area (hypothalamus-POA) in mice.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In fact, genetic analyses revealed that the drug altered the way genes were turned on and off in certain cells types in the hypothalamus.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Using advanced genetic analysis, the researchers found that tamoxifen significantly altered gene activity in a specific brain region known as the hypothalamus-POA.
allowed_evidence_spans: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that tamoxifen treatment induces widespread gene expression changes in the hypothalamus and preoptic area ( hypothalamus-POA ) .

Using single-cell RNA sequencing , we find that tamoxifen alters transcriptomes in the hypothalamus-POA , consistent with the hypothesis that tamoxifen treatment alters central nervous system function ( Eberling et al . , 2004; Gibbs et al . , 2014; Denk et al . , 2015 ) .

Profiling genome-wide expression changes of individual cells in the hypothalamus-POA using Drop-seq , a droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing technology , revealed transcriptional changes induced by tamoxifen in multiple cell types .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Neurons and ependymal cells in the hypothalamus-POA were most sensitive to tamoxifen administration, showing the highest numbers of differentially expressed genes.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Among all cell types , neurons and ependymal cells were most sensitive to tamoxifen administration , as indicated by the number of significantly induced and repressed genes ( Figure 3D ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: These expression changes are dependent on estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), as conditional knockout of ERα in the hypothalamus-POA ablates or reverses tamoxifen-induced gene expression.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Tamoxifen-induced gene expression changes in the hypothalamus-POA are dependent on estrogen receptor alpha (ERα).
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that these gene expression changes rely on estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), as removing ERα in the hypothalamus-POA either eliminated or reversed the effects of tamoxifen on gene expression.
allowed_evidence_spans: These expression changes are dependent on estrogen receptor alpha ( ERα ) , as conditional knockout of ERα in the hypothalamus-POA ablates or reverses tamoxifen-induced gene expression .
These expression changes are dependent on estrogen receptor alpha ( ERα ) , as conditional knockout of ERα in the hypothalamus-POA ablates or reverses tamoxifen-induced gene expression .
Instead it ablated or reversed the direction of a significant number of the tamoxifen-induced gene expression changes that were observed in the wild-type hypothalamus-POA .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Accordingly, ERα-deficient mice do not exhibit tamoxifen-induced changes in temperature, bone, or movement.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: ERα-deficient mice do not exhibit tamoxifen-induced changes in temperature, bone, or movement.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Crucially, mice whose hypothalamus and preoptic area lacked estrogen receptors did not experience these behavioral and biological alterations.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Consistent with the genetic findings, mice lacking ERα did not show the tamoxifen-induced changes in temperature, bone, or movement.
allowed_evidence_spans: Accordingly , ERα-deficient mice do not exhibit tamoxifen-induced changes in temperature , bone , or movement .

Finally , we show that ERα expression in the hypothalamus-POA is necessary for the tamoxifen-induced chances in gene expression in the hypothalamus-POA and the effects on thermoregulation , bone density , and movement .
Knockout of ERα in the hypothalamus-POA largely blocked the effect of tamoxifen on bone physiology as well .

Although the effects of estrogens on thermoregulation are probably multifaceted and complex, it is clear that ablating ERα is sufficient to abrogate the effects of tamoxifen on core body temperature and tail skin temperature in mice.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: These findings provide mechanistic insight into the effects of tamoxifen on the hypothalamus-POA and indicate that ERα mediates several physiological effects of tamoxifen treatment in mice.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: ERα mediates several physiological effects of tamoxifen treatment in mice.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The findings by Zhang et al. help to understand how the side effects of tamoxifen emerge, singling out estrogen receptors in particular brain regions.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Overall, the study provides a mechanistic understanding of how tamoxifen affects the hypothalamus-POA and highlights the crucial role of ERα in mediating its physiological side effects in mice.
allowed_evidence_spans: These findings provide mechanistic insight into the effects of tamoxifen on the hypothalamus-POA and indicate that ERα mediates several physiological effects of tamoxifen treatment in mice .
Together , these findings suggest that tamoxifen treatment modulates ERα signaling in the central nervous system to alter fundamental aspects of physiology and health .
Together , these data indicate an indispensable role for ERα in the molecular and physiological response to tamoxifen treatment in mice .

Nevertheless, conditional knockout of ERα in the hypothalamus-POA blocked the majority of the physiological changes observed in wild-type mice by tamoxifen, indicating a pivotal role of ERα in mediating the homeostatic effects of tamoxifen.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer (smFRET) is an adaptable method for studying the structure and dynamics of biomolecules.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer (smFRET) is a method used to study the structure and dynamics of biomolecules.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: An important technique for studying protein flexibility is known as single molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET).
evidence_rows.lay_context: smFRET is a technique that allows researchers to observe the movements and interactions of individual biomolecules, which can be missed by other methods that look at average shapes.
allowed_evidence_spans: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer ( smFRET ) is an adaptable method for studying the structure and dynamics of biomolecules .

Capturing the real-time readouts of nanometer-scale distances of individual biomolecules by smFRET allows the direct observations of dynamics , interactions , and intermediates of stochastic non-accumulating events , as well as dynamic equilibria between unsynchronized molecules , all of which are obscured in ensemble averaging techniques ( Dimura et al . , 2016; Hellenkamp et al . , 2018; Holmstrom et al . , 2019; Juette et al . , 2016; Newton et al . , 2019; Preus et al . , 2015; Roy et al . , 2008; Schuler and Eaton , 2008; Stella et al . , 2018 ) .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: FRET is the only method for studying protein flexibility.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The development of high throughput methodologies and the growth of commercial instrumentation have outpaced the development of rapid, standardized, and automated methodologies to objectively analyze the wealth of produced data.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The development of high-throughput smFRET methodologies and commercial instrumentation has outpaced the development of rapid, standardized, and automated data analysis methods.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Advances in the instruments used to perform FRET have made observing the motion of individual proteins more widely accessible to non-specialists, but the analysis of the data that these instruments produce still requires a high level of expertise.
evidence_rows.lay_context: While smFRET instruments have become more accessible, analyzing the large amounts of data they produce is still challenging, often requiring manual supervision and expert tuning of thresholds, which can be time-consuming and introduce bias.
allowed_evidence_spans: The development of high throughput methodologies and the growth of commercial instrumentation have outpaced the development of rapid , standardized , and automated methodologies to objectively analyze the wealth of produced data .

Existing software ( Greenfeld et al . , 2012; Hellenkamp et al . , 2018; Hon and Gonzalez , 2019; Juette et al . , 2016; Preus et al . , 2015; Stella et al . , 2018 ) by single-molecule labs can simplify the tedious and time-consuming selection of traces and were recently expanded to large datasets ( Juette et al . , 2016 ) albeit requiring some form of manual supervision and hyper-parameter tuning selecting the proper thresholds by an expert user . This need for human intervention could potentially be subjected to cognitive biases especially by less experienced users and could limit the expansion of smFRET to classic biology labs .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: smFRET data analysis is impossible without experts.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Here we present DeepFRET, an automated, open-source standalone solution based on deep learning, where the only crucial human intervention in transiting from raw microscope images to histograms of biomolecule behavior, is a user-adjustable quality threshold.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: DeepFRET is an automated, open-source, standalone solution based on deep learning for analyzing smFRET data, requiring only a user-adjustable quality threshold as crucial human intervention.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Thomsen et al. have developed a new way to automate the data analysis. They used machine learning technology to recognize, filter and characterize data so as to produce reliable results, with the user only needing to perform a couple of steps.
evidence_rows.lay_context: DeepFRET is a new software that uses deep learning to automate the analysis of smFRET data, significantly reducing the need for human input to just setting a quality threshold.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here we present DeepFRET , an automated , open-source standalone solution based on deep learning , where the only crucial human intervention in transiting from raw microscope images to histograms of biomolecule behavior , is a user-adjustable quality threshold .

Here we present DeepFRET , an automated , open-source standalone solution based on deep learning , where the only crucial human intervention in transiting from raw microscope images to histograms of biomolecule behavior , is a user-adjustable quality threshold .

The fact that DeepFRET does so only requiring a score threshold , as a sole human intervention , demonstrates its strength as a novel smFRET analysis method and its potential to form a reference against which the quality of the data and the structural biology
forbidden_overgeneralizations: DeepFRET requires no human intervention at all.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Integrating standard features of smFRET analysis, DeepFRET consequently outputs the common kinetic information metrics.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: DeepFRET outputs common kinetic information metrics by integrating standard features of smFRET analysis.
evidence_rows.lay_context: DeepFRET is designed to provide the same key measurements about molecular movement and behavior that researchers expect from smFRET analysis, but in an automated way.
allowed_evidence_spans: Integrating standard features of smFRET analysis , DeepFRET consequently outputs the common kinetic information metrics .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Its classification accuracy on ground truth data reached >95% outperforming human operators and commonly used threshold, only requiring ~1% of the time.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: DeepFRET achieved over 95% classification accuracy on ground truth data, outperforming human operators and commonly used threshold methods, while requiring approximately 1% of the time.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This new analysis approach could help expand the use of single-molecule FRET to different fields, allowing researchers to investigate the importance of protein flexibility for certain diseases, or to better understand the roles that proteins have in a cell.
evidence_rows.lay_context: DeepFRET is highly accurate, classifying data correctly more than 95% of the time, which is better than both human experts and traditional analysis methods, and it does so in a fraction of the time.

DeepFRET classification accuracy consistently outperformed trace selection using commonly published thresholds . Similarly , it supersedes the selection accuracy of human operators and importantly , only requiring a fraction of the time ( minutes versus weeks if traces are manually selected ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Its precise and rapid operation on real data demonstrates DeepFRET’s capacity to objectively quantify biomolecular dynamics and the potential to contribute to benchmarking smFRET for dynamic structural biology.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: DeepFRET's precise and rapid operation on real data demonstrates its capacity to objectively quantify biomolecular dynamics and its potential to contribute to benchmarking smFRET for dynamic structural biology.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This new analysis approach could help expand the use of single-molecule FRET to different fields, allowing researchers to investigate the importance of protein flexibility for certain diseases, or to better understand the roles that proteins have in a cell.
evidence_rows.lay_context: DeepFRET's speed and accuracy mean it can objectively measure how biomolecules move and change, and it could help set new standards for how smFRET data is evaluated across different labs and experiments.
allowed_evidence_spans: Its precise and rapid operation on real data demonstrates DeepFRET’s capacity to objectively quantify biomolecular dynamics and the potential to contribute to benchmarking smFRET for dynamic structural biology .

The fact that DeepFRET does so only requiring a score threshold , as a sole human intervention , demonstrates its strength as a novel smFRET analysis method and its potential to form a reference against which the quality of the data and the structural biology insights are benchmarked .

We anticipate that DeepFRET , combined with the advent of commercial single-molecule instruments , will contribute in materializing the smFRET as a robust mainstream toolkit for structural biology labs .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: DeepFRET will solve all problems in structural biology.

evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Asymptomatic carriage of Streptococcus pneumoniae in the nasopharynx is a necessary condition for the disease to occur.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: it lives harmlessly in the nose, and is particularly common in children and the elderly. The longer the bacteria live in the nose before being killed by the immune system, the more likely they are to be transmitted to another person.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Before causing disease, S. pneumoniae must first colonize the nasopharynx without symptoms. The duration of this carriage is important for understanding disease transmission, but its variability has only been understood at the serotype level.
allowed_evidence_spans: Asymptomatic carriage in the nasopharynx is a prerequisite for disease , but variability in its duration is currently only understood at the serotype level .

The pneumococcus spends most of the transmission cycle in the nasopharynx , and so understanding and predicting the amount of time spent in this niche is critical for understanding this bacterium's epidemiology , and therefore controlling transmission ( Abdullahi et al . , 2012a; Melegaro et al . , 2007 ) .

One factor that is known to strongly associate with carriage duration is serotype: as capsular polysaccharides are important in bacterial physiology and determining host immune response , different serotypes have different clearance and acquisition rates ( Abdullahi et al . , 2012a; Hill et al . , 2010; Högberg et al . , 2007; Melegaro et al . , 2004; Turner et al . , 2012 ) .
However , the overall and relative contributions of these sequence variations to carriage rate have not yet been characterised .

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Lees et al . have developed a mathematical model to calculate how long the bacteria are carried in the nose before they are cleared away , and compared it with the genomic data of the bacteria . For this , over 14 , 000 nose swabs from almost 600 children were collected over a two-year period .
evidence_rows.lay_context: To understand the genetic contributions to carriage duration, researchers developed a model to calculate the duration of S. pneumoniae carriage episodes from longitudinal swab data and integrated this with whole genome sequence data. This involved analyzing data from 598 unvaccinated children over two years.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here we developed a model to calculate the duration of carriage episodes from longitudinal swab data , and combined these results with whole genome sequence data .

By developing models for longitudinal swab data and combining the results with whole genome sequence data we have quantified and mapped the genetic contribution to the carriage duration of S . pneumoniae .
For 598 unvaccinated children up to 24 swabs taken over a two year period were available , an extension on the previous study ( Turner et al . , 2012 , 2013a ) .

To estimate carriage duration from the longitudinal swab data we constructed a set of hidden Markov models ( HMMs ) with hidden states corresponding to whether a child was carrying a serotype at a given time point , and observed states corresponding to whether a positive swab was observed for this serotype at this time point .

However , the study of this fundamental aspect was largely abandoned so far , due to tacitly conceiving the cytosolic pool as a passive supply of individual integrin adhesome proteins . In this work we challenged this view by systematic FCCS and FRAP measurements .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Stationary focal adhesions release symmetrically the same types of protein complexes that they recruit, thereby keeping the cytosolic pool of building blocks spatiotemporally uniform.

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: these building blocks do not change when they are exchanged between the cytosol and the adhesion site: this means that they can be re-used repeatedly and accurately.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that focal adhesions, a type of adhesion site, release the same protein complexes they take in. This 'symmetric exchange' helps maintain a consistent supply of building blocks in the cytosol.
allowed_evidence_spans: Stationary focal adhesions release symmetrically the same types of protein complexes that they recruit , thereby keeping the cytosolic pool of building blocks spatiotemporally uniform.

These results indicate that there are no spatial gradients of different (i.e., primed) protein complexes around focal adhesions, indicating that stationary focal adhesions release the same types of complexes that they recruited.
In contrast , a symmetric exchange ensures a spatially uniform pool of building blocks for adhesion sites and prevents any communication between these sites via primed components .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We conclude a model in which multi-protein building blocks enable rapid and modular self-assembly of adhesion sites and symmetric exchange of these building blocks preserves their specifications and thus the assembly logic of the system.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Multi-protein building blocks enable rapid and modular self-assembly of adhesion sites.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: These can make the construction of cell-matrix adhesion sites quicker and more accurate by reducing the number of steps in the self-assembly process.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The use of multi-protein building blocks allows for faster and more organized assembly of adhesion sites, as fewer steps are needed compared to assembling individual proteins.
allowed_evidence_spans: We conclude a model in which multi-protein building blocks enable rapid and modular self-assembly of adhesion sites and symmetric exchange of these building blocks preserves their specifications and thus the assembly logic of the system .
Multi-protein building blocks , in comparison to single-protein building blocks , reduce the number of steps required for self-assembly of adhesion sites .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We conclude a model in which multi-protein building blocks enable rapid and modular self-assembly of adhesion sites and symmetric exchange of these building blocks preserves their specifications and thus the assembly logic of the system.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Symmetric exchange of multi-protein building blocks preserves their specifications and the assembly logic of the system.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In addition, under most circumstances, these building blocks do not change when they are exchanged between the cytosol and the adhesion site: this means that they can be re-used repeatedly and accurately.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The symmetric exchange mechanism ensures that the multi-protein building blocks maintain their specific characteristics, which is crucial for the correct and efficient assembly of adhesion sites.
allowed_evidence_spans: We conclude a model in which multi-protein building blocks enable rapid and modular self-assembly of adhesion sites and symmetric exchange of these building blocks preserves their specifications and thus the assembly logic of the system .

Symmetric material exchange between adhesion sites and cytosol satisfies this requirement by ensuring that building blocks will enter and exit adhesion sites without being altered. Symmetric material exchange between adhesion sites and cytosol retains the wiring of the building blocks and therefore retains the assembly logic and switchability of the system.
Since adhesion sites are self-assembled structures , a standardized pool of building blocks is essential for their correct and efficient assembly .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Intriguingly, categorization performance was markedly improved when locations were revealed to participants by an optimal Bayesian active sensor algorithm.

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The model could also work out the next best fixation location that would maximize the amount of information that could be collected.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The researchers developed a Bayesian active sensor (BAS) algorithm to choose the next fixation location that would maximally reduce uncertainty in the category, thereby providing an optimal benchmark for human performance.
allowed_evidence_spans: Intriguingly, categorization performance was markedly improved when locations were revealed to participants by an optimal Bayesian active sensor algorithm.

To be able to rigorously assess how close our participants were to optimal sensing , we developed a Bayesian active sensor ( BAS ) algorithm which is optimal in minimizing categorization error with every single revealing .
That is , for our task , the aim of BAS is to choose the next fixation location , x* , so as to maximally reduce uncertainty in the category ( MacKay , 1992 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: By using a combination of a Bayesian ideal observer and the active sensor algorithm, we estimate that a major portion of this apparent suboptimality of fixation locations arises from prior biases, perceptual noise and inaccuracies in eye movements, and the central process of selecting fixation locations is around 70% efficient in our task.

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Furthermore, it suggests that the inefficiencies are largely caused by imperfect vision and inaccurate eye movements.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study estimated that the central process of selecting fixation locations was around 70% efficient, suggesting that other factors like prior biases, perceptual noise, and inaccuracies in eye movements contribute significantly to the observed suboptimality.
allowed_evidence_spans: By using a combination of a Bayesian ideal observer and the active sensor algorithm, we estimate that a major portion of this apparent suboptimality of fixation locations arises from prior biases, perceptual noise and inaccuracies in eye movements, and the central process of selecting fixation locations is around 70% efficient in our task.
This suggests that the central component of choosing where to fixate was around 70% efficient in our participants , and a large component of suboptimality arose due to other processes .

our results suggest that this suboptimality in participants’ performance was to a large part due to prior biases , perception noise , and saccadic inaccuracies constraining the selection of fixation locations rather than an inefficient active sensing strategy .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Our results suggest that participants select eye movements with the goal of maximizing information about abstract categories that require the integration of information from multiple locations.

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Yang, Lengyel and Wolpert’s findings indicate that we combine information from multiple locations to direct our eye movements so that we can maximize the information we collect from our surroundings.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study's task specifically required integrating low-level visual information from multiple locations to form an abstract category, highlighting the importance of a closed-loop interaction between perception and eye movement planning for maximal efficiency.
allowed_evidence_spans: Our results suggest that participants select eye movements with the goal of maximizing information about abstract categories that require the integration of information from multiple locations.

For maximal efficiency, this requires a closed loop interaction between perception, which integrates information from the locations already fixated with prior knowledge about the prevalence of different animals and their fur patterns, and thus maintains beliefs about which animal might be present in the image, and the planning of eye movement, which should direct the next fixation at a location which has potentially the most information relevant for the categorization (Figure 1).

Second , by using a pattern categorization task we could ensure that no single location was especially informative but that the task required an integration of information from multiple locations both to select the next eye movement and to solve the task , and specifically that a closed-loop strategy was necessary for solving the task efficiently .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Lab-infected flies manifest the moribund behaviors characteristic of E. muscae infection: hours before death, they climb upward, extend their proboscides, affixing in place, then raise their wings, clearing a path for infectious spores to launch from their abdomens.

A fly infected with E . muscae exhibits a characteristic set of fungus-induced behaviors: shortly before sunset on its final day of life , the fly climbs to a high location ( a behavior known as ‘summiting’ ) , extends its proboscis and becomes affixed to the surface via fungal holdfasts , hyphal growths that emerge through the mouthparts ( Roy et al . , 2006; Balazy , 1984; Krasnoff et al . , 1995 ) .
The fly’s wings then lift up and away from its dorsal abdomen , striking a final death pose that is thought to be ideal for fungal dispersal ( Krasnoff et al . , 1995 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: A depolarizing 'leak' current supports this firing pattern, but its molecular basis remains poorly understood.

evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: A current of positively charged ions constantly flows into the spontaneously active SNr neurons and enables them to fire constantly.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This 'leak' current is a continuous flow of ions that keeps the neuron's membrane potential depolarized, allowing it to fire action potentials spontaneously.
allowed_evidence_spans: A depolarizing 'leak' current supports this firing pattern , but its molecular basis remains poorly understood .

Electrophysiological studies of spontaneously active neurons have frequently reported the presence of a tonic current that maintains these neurons at a more depolarized membrane potential and likely allows them to continuously fire action potentials ( Atherton and Bevan , 2005; Raman et al . , 2000; Jackson et al . , 2004; Taddese and Bean , 2002; Khaliq and Bean , 2010 ) .
However , the molecular identity of the channel ( s ) that carry this leak current in many spontaneously firing neurons remains an open question .

evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The researchers used single-cell RNA sequencing to determine the transcriptome of individual mouse SNr neurons to understand how they maintain tonic activity.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Lutas et al. have now used single-cell RNA sequencing to study SNr neurons from mice and investigate which ion channel the positive ion current flows through.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Single-cell RNA sequencing allows researchers to identify all the genes expressed in individual cells, providing clues about the proteins, such as ion channels, that are present and functional in those cells.
allowed_evidence_spans: To understand how SNr neurons maintain tonic activity , we used single-cell RNA sequencing to determine the transcriptome of individual mouse SNr neurons .

To clarify which NSSC are expressed by SNr neurons , we chose an unbiased approach that took advantage of advances in RNA sequencing ( RNA-seq ) technology to obtain whole transcriptome gene expression data from individual SNr neurons .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: RNA sequencing directly measures protein levels.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We discovered that SNr neurons express the sodium leak channel, NALCN, and that SNr neurons lacking NALCN have impaired spontaneous firing.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: SNr neurons express the sodium leak channel, NALCN, and SNr neurons lacking NALCN have impaired spontaneous firing.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The RNA sequences revealed that the neurons have the gene for an ion channel known as NALCN. Recordings of the firing rate of neurons in slices of mouse brain showed that SNr neurons without this channel did not fire as often as SNr neurons with the channel.
evidence_rows.lay_context: NALCN is a specific type of ion channel that allows sodium ions to 'leak' into the cell, contributing to the depolarizing current needed for spontaneous firing.
allowed_evidence_spans: We discovered that SNr neurons express the sodium leak channel , NALCN , and that SNr neurons lacking NALCN have impaired spontaneous firing .

Consistent with an important role of NALCN in maintaining spontaneous firing of SNr neurons, the spontaneous firing rate of NALCN KO SNr neurons was significantly lower than control SNr neurons (Figure 5C, D).
forbidden_overgeneralizations: NALCN is the only channel involved in SNr firing.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The spontaneous firing rate of NALCN knockout (KO) SNr neurons was significantly lower than control SNr neurons.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Consistent with an important role of NALCN in maintaining spontaneous firing of SNr neurons, the spontaneous firing rate of NALCN KO SNr neurons was significantly lower than control SNr neurons (Figure 5C, D).

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: In addition, NALCN is involved in the modulation of excitability by changes in glycolysis and by activation of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: NALCN is involved in the modulation of SNr neuron excitability by changes in glycolysis and by activation of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Neurotransmitters (chemicals that alter the ability of neurons to fire) and changes in cell metabolism had less of an effect on the firing rate of SNr neurons that lacked the NALCN channel than they do on normal neurons.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This means NALCN not only contributes to baseline firing but also helps SNr neurons adjust their activity in response to metabolic changes (like energy availability from glycolysis) and signals from other neurons via muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
allowed_evidence_spans: In addition , NALCN is involved in the modulation of excitability by changes in glycolysis and by activation of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors .
We find that it is important for regulation of SNr neuronal excitability in response to changes in glycolysis , an effect we had seen previously when investigating
These results indicate that NALCN , but not TRPC3 , is important for the regulation of SNr neuron excitability by mAChR activation .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: NALCN is the only channel modulated by glycolysis or muscarinic receptors.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Our findings suggest that disruption of NALCN could impair the basal ganglia circuit, which may underlie the severe motor deficits in humans carrying mutations in NALCN.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Disruption of NALCN could impair the basal ganglia circuit, potentially underlying severe motor deficits in humans with NALCN mutations.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: These findings may help explain why people with mutations in the NALCN gene have movement disorders, as the substantia nigra pars reticulata plays an important role in orchestrating complex movements.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Since the basal ganglia circuit is crucial for motor control, impaired NALCN function could lead to movement disorders observed in individuals with NALCN gene mutations.
allowed_evidence_spans: Our findings suggest that disruption of NALCN could impair the basal ganglia circuit , which may underlie the severe motor deficits in humans carrying mutations in NALCN .

Recent studies have found that mutations in NALCN result in severe motor and cognitive deficits in humans ( Chong et al . , 2015; Aoyagi et al . , 2015; Al-Sayed et al . , 2013; Köroğlu et al . , 2013; Fukai et al . , 2016 ) .
Our finding that SNr neurons require NALCN for appropriate tonic firing , suggests that NALCN mutations could contribute to basal ganglia related motor disorders.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: NALCN mutations cause all motor deficits.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Human mutations in NALCN lead to severe motor and cognitive deficits.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Furthermore , our results identify key cellular responses that are impaired in the absence of NALCN , and may have therapeutic value as human mutations in NALCN lead to severe motor and cognitive deficits ( Chong et al . , 2015; Aoyagi et al . , 2015; Al-Sayed et al . , 2013; Köroğlu et al . , 2013; Fukai et al . , 2016 ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The roles of chance, contingency, and necessity in evolution are unresolved because they have never been assessed in a single system or on timescales relevant to historical evolution.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The roles of chance, contingency, and necessity in evolution are unresolved because they have never been assessed in a single system or on timescales relevant to historical evolution.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: One of the most fundamental and unresolved questions in evolutionary biology is whether the outcomes of evolution are predictable.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Scientists are still trying to understand how much of evolution is due to random chance, how much is influenced by past events (contingency), and how much is predetermined (necessity). This is hard to study because evolution happened long ago and cannot be easily replayed.
allowed_evidence_spans: The roles of chance , contingency , and necessity in evolution are unresolved because they have never been assessed in a single system or on timescales relevant to historical evolution .

The extent to which biological diversity is the necessary result of optimization by natural selection or the unpredictable product of random events and historical contingency is one of evolutionary biology’s most fundamental and unresolved questions.

the relative importance of these factors during evolutionary history remains unresolved because they have never been measured in the same system , and their effects over long evolutionary time scales have not been characterized .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The authors combined ancestral protein reconstruction and a new continuous evolution technology to mutate and select proteins in the B-cell lymphoma-2 (BCL-2) family to acquire protein–protein interaction specificities that occurred during animal evolution.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The authors combined ancestral protein reconstruction and a new continuous evolution technology to study protein evolution.

evidence_rows.lay_context: To investigate these questions, researchers used a new experimental method. They reconstructed ancient proteins from the BCL-2 family and used a continuous evolution technology to observe how these proteins evolved new binding specificities, mimicking changes that happened naturally over animal evolution.
allowed_evidence_spans: We combined ancestral protein reconstruction and a new continuous evolution technology to mutate and select proteins in the B-cell lymphoma-2 ( BCL-2 ) family to acquire protein–protein interaction specificities that occurred during animal evolution .

Here we implement this strategy using the B-cell lymphoma-2 ( BCL-2 ) protein family as a model system and the specificity of protein–protein interactions ( PPIs ) as the target of selection .
To drive the evolution of new PPI specificities , we developed a new high-throughput phage-assisted continuous evolution ( PACE ) system

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: By replicating evolutionary trajectories from multiple ancestral proteins, we found that contingency generated over long historical timescales steadily erased necessity and overwhelmed chance as the primary cause of acquired sequence variation; trajectories launched from phylogenetically distant proteins yielded virtually no common mutations, even under strong and identical selection pressures.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Contingency generated over long historical timescales steadily erased necessity and overwhelmed chance as the primary cause of acquired sequence variation.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The outcomes of evolution were almost completely unpredictable: trajectories initiated from the same ancestral protein produced proteins with very different sequences, and proteins launched from different ancestral starting points were even more dissimilar.
evidence_rows.lay_context: By replaying evolution many times from different ancestral proteins, the researchers discovered that past events (contingency) became the main driver of how protein sequences changed over long periods, making the outcomes less predictable and overriding the effects of pure chance or necessity.
allowed_evidence_spans: By replicating evolutionary trajectories from multiple ancestral proteins , we found that contingency generated over long historical timescales steadily erased necessity and overwhelmed chance as the primary cause of acquired sequence variation
trajectories launched from phylogenetically distant proteins yielded virtually no common mutations , even under strong and identical selection pressures .

The mutations that rose to high frequency during experimental evolution were almost completely different among evolutionary trajectories initiated from historical starting points separated by long phylogenetic distances .
Contingency’s effect was even larger than that of chance , increasing Vt by an average of 80% across all pairs of starting points compared to Vg when selecting for a new function .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Trajectories launched from phylogenetically distant proteins yielded virtually no common mutations, even under strong and identical selection pressures.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: trajectories launched from phylogenetically distant proteins yielded virtually no common mutations , even under strong and identical selection pressures .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Chance arose because many sets of mutations could alter specificity at any timepoint; contingency arose because historical substitutions changed these sets.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Chance arose because many sets of mutations could alter specificity at any timepoint.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Early chance events influenced each protein’s evolution in an unpredictable way by opening and closing the paths available to it in the future.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Chance played a role because there were many different ways (sets of mutations) a protein could change its binding specificity at any given moment. Contingency, on the other hand, meant that previous changes (historical substitutions) altered which of these mutational paths were available later.
allowed_evidence_spans: Chance arose because many sets of mutations could alter specificity at any timepoint
contingency arose because historical substitutions changed these sets .

Contingency therefore arose because historical substitutions that occurred during the intervals between ancestral proteins made specificity-changing mutations either deleterious or functionally inconsequential when introduced into genetic backgrounds that existed before or after those in which the mutations occurred .
For chance to strongly influence the outcomes of adaptive evolution , multiple paths to a selected phenotype must be accessible with similar probabilities of being taken .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: only one path to evolution exists

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Our results suggest that patterns of variation in BCL-2 sequences – and likely other proteins, too – are idiosyncratic products of a particular and unpredictable course of historical events.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Patterns of variation in BCL-2 sequences are idiosyncratic products of a particular and unpredictable course of historical events.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The results suggest that BCL-2 proteins, in all their various forms, are unique products of a particular, unpredictable course of history set in motion by ancient chance events.
evidence_rows.lay_context: These findings indicate that the specific ways BCL-2 protein sequences have changed over time are unique and could not have been predicted, suggesting that the path of evolution for these proteins, and likely others, is shaped by a specific and unpredictable series of past events.
allowed_evidence_spans: Our results suggest that patterns of variation in BCL-2 sequences – and likely other proteins , too – are idiosyncratic products of a particular and unpredictable course of historical events .
Together , contingency generated across long phylogenetic timescales and chance therefore make sequence evolution in the BCL-2 family almost entirely unpredictable .
We studied a particular protein family as a model , but we expect that qualitatively similar results may apply to many other proteins .

Our observations suggest that sequence–structure–function associations apparent in sequence alignments are to a significant degree the result of contingent constraints that were transiently imposed or removed by chance events during history
must_use_terms: particular and unpredictable course of historical events

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The study used a particular protein family as a model, but qualitatively similar results are expected to apply to many other proteins.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: We studied a particular protein family as a model , but we expect that qualitatively similar results may apply to many other proteins .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Early development of many animals is characterized by rapid cleavages that dramatically decrease cell size, but how the mitotic spindle adapts to changing cell dimensions is not understood.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: During early animal development, rapid cell divisions lead to a dramatic decrease in cell size, but the mechanism by which the mitotic spindle adapts to these changing cell dimensions is not understood.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Explain the problem: cells divide rapidly without growth, becoming smaller, so the spindle must also become smaller.
evidence_rows.lay_context: In the earliest stages of development, animal cells undergo multiple rounds of division without growth, transforming a single fertilized egg into many smaller cells. The mitotic spindle, which separates chromosomes during cell division, must also become smaller to ensure proper chromosome distribution in these decreasing cell sizes.
allowed_evidence_spans: Early development of many animals is characterized by rapid cleavages that dramatically decrease cell size
but how the mitotic spindle adapts to changing cell dimensions is not understood.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: To identify mechanisms that scale the spindle during Xenopus laevis embryogenesis, we established an in vitro system using cytoplasmic extracts prepared from embryos that recapitulates in vivo spindle size differences between stage 3 (4 cells, 37 µm) and stage 8 (~4000 cells, 18 µm).
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: To investigate spindle scaling mechanisms during Xenopus laevis embryogenesis, an in vitro system was developed using cytoplasmic extracts from embryos, which successfully replicated the in vivo spindle size differences observed between stage 3 (4 cells, 37 µm) and stage 8 (~4000 cells, 18 µm).

evidence_rows.lay_context: The researchers used Xenopus laevis, a frog with large embryos, as a model organism. They prepared cytoplasmic extracts from embryos at two distinct developmental stages: stage 3 (with 4 cells, each 37 µm) and stage 8 (with approximately 4000 cells, each 18 µm). This in vitro system allowed them to study how spindle size changes as cells become smaller.
allowed_evidence_spans: To identify mechanisms that scale the spindle during Xenopus laevis embryogenesis

we established an in vitro system using cytoplasmic extracts prepared from embryos that recapitulates in vivo spindle size differences between stage 3 ( 4 cells , 37 µm ) and stage 8 ( ∼4000 cells , 18 µm ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: We identified the kinesin-13 kif2a as a driver of developmental spindle scaling whose microtubule-destabilizing activity is inhibited in stage 3 spindles by the transport receptor importin α, and activated in stage 8 when importin α partitions to a membrane pool.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The kinesin-13 kif2a was identified as a key driver of developmental spindle scaling; its microtubule-destabilizing activity is inhibited in stage 3 spindles by the transport receptor importin α, but activated in stage 8 when importin α moves to a membrane pool.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Explain the roles of kif2a and importin-α in controlling spindle size.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study found that two proteins, kif2a and importin α, control spindle size. Kif2a destabilizes microtubules, which are components of the spindle, causing them to shorten. In early stage 3 embryos, importin α inhibits kif2a's activity. However, in later stage 8 embryos, importin α moves to the cell membrane, freeing kif2a to destabilize microtubules and reduce spindle size.
allowed_evidence_spans: We identified the kinesin-13 kif2a as a driver of developmental spindle scaling
whose microtubule-destabilizing activity is inhibited in stage 3 spindles by the transport receptor importin α
and activated in stage 8 when importin α partitions to a membrane pool .
This occurs through redistribution of importin α from the cytoplasm to a membrane fraction .
